blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — Police arrested 76 people in 20 operations against illegal gambling across the Ilocos Region from Sept. 1 to 6, the Police Regional Office 1 (PRO 1) said.
The operations resulted in the confiscation of P33,457 in alleged bet money, according to PRO 1.
Police said the operations targeted various forms of illegal gambling, including illegal number games, jueteng, dice games, coin games and sports betting.

Brig. Gen. Crisaleo Tolentino, PRO 1 regional director, said the campaign against illegal gambling would remain intensified, urging police personnel and the public to remain vigilant against such activities.

“Our fight against illegal gambling does not end with these arrests. We will sustain our operations and strengthen our presence in communities to prevent these unlawful activities from spreading,” Tolentino said.
He also called on communities to cooperate with the police to keep their neighborhoods safe, peaceful and orderly. —Kenneth P. Tabin/Contributor /das

articles.title: Romualdez directed to attend Sandiganbayan hearing on Sept. 10, 2026
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has directed former Speaker Martin Romualdez to appear before a hearing on September 10, 2026 on his motion for continued hospital confinement.

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 10:00pm
The Sandiganbayan has directed former Speaker Martin Romualdez to appear before a hearing on September 10, 2026 on his motion for continued hospital confinement.

Romualdez has remained hospitalized at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City since Monday, when police served a warrant of arrest issued by the anti-graft court over a P7.4 billion plunder case.
Late Monday, his camp filed a petition before the Sandiganbayan's Third Division to grant him "continued hospital confinement" due to health issues.
"Accused Romualdez is directed to appear before the court should his condition permit," the Sandiganbayan said.
"Accused Romualdez and/or his doctors are likewise directed to furnish the court during the said hearing the results of all pertinent medical examinations of accused Romualdez," it added.

“It should be emphasized that the custody of accused Romualdez belongs to the court. If there are concerns regarding the accused's medical condition, it is only this court that can determine whether such condition affects the implementation of the warrant, the confinement of the accused at a hospital, or his commitment to a jail facility. Considering the allegations in accused Romualdez's Manifestation and Urgent Motion which raise serious concerns on his medical condition, the court deems it proper to set the Manifestation and Urgent Motion for hearing on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning,” the Sandiganbayan also said.

The Third Division order also directed the Clerk of Court to "issue subpoena ad testificandum to Dr. Rody Sy, Dr. Rogelio Libarres, Dr. Kurt Allen V. Sibayan, and Dr. Rosalio P. Torres of Cardinal for the hearing on September 10, 2026, and to furnish PNP CIDG-NCR, as well as the foregoing doctors copies of this Order." —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Police were told night before Dover unrest that far-right agitators had converged on village
articles.summary:
Details passed to Kent police after far-right activists heard in pub boasting about going to to Dover to ‘attack Muslims’

Police were told the night before far-right agitators blocked roads…

blocks.text: Police were told the night before far-right agitators blocked roads into Dover that those involved had converged on a village 18 miles away and planned to use it as a launchpad, it has emerged.
People in Preston-next-Wingham told of how hundreds of men had started to arrive in the village of just over 920 residents on Friday afternoon and in effect “took over” the village.

At least one person is understood to have sought to pass on details to counter-terrorism police after people heard the far-right activists boasting in the local pub that they intended to go to Dover and “attack Muslims”.

The information was passed on to police but little or no interest was shown in the tipoff, according to the anti-fascist group Hope Not Hate, who spoke to the person. Others reported careless and illegal parking to the police but no action was said to have been taken.

The claims have raised fresh questions about Kent police’s handling of the protest, in which hundreds descended on Dover at 7am and which the force described as “spontaneous”. No arrests were made during the action, which involved hundreds of black-clad masked men standing in the middle of roads and led to access to the port of Dover being blocked for several hours.
Roger Gale, the MP for Herne Bay and Sandwich, who lives in Preston-next-Wingham, said the unrest in Dover on Saturday was clearly not “spontaneous”.

He said that the village in Kent was unusually full of cars on Friday night and that a local car park and the recreation ground was still full of vehicles on Saturday morning, prompting him to call 999.

Gale said: “A local councillor took photographs of the number plates and they should be able work back from those to establish who owns the cars. I called 999 at around 9.30am on Saturday and two officers came over quite quickly.

“I am going to write to the chief constable to ask what they are going to do with this information. There were roughly 50 cars in the car park and the recreation ground and more on the road. [What happened in Dover] was not spontaneous. It was carefully coordinated. Those participating were transported from the village to Dover, most likely in Luton vans.”

Gale was not aware of calls being made to the police on Friday but he added that he knew that conversations among participants in Saturday’s unrest had been overheard in the village pub on Friday night.

Kent police have been approached for comment. The force said this week that the unrest on Saturday involved about 200 people and had “developed rapidly”. It added that the protest was treated in line with national guidance as spontaneous based on the information available to the force at the time.
after newsletter promotion

The action was organised by Daniel Thomas, a long-term associate of the far right activist known as Tommy Robinson. Thomas, who has established an umbrella grouping called Patriot Platform, was also linked to a blockade in Portsmouth the following day.
One person who lives in Preston-next-Wingham told Hope Not Hate: “There were hundreds of them. They took over the place.
“They were literally parking everywhere. They parked in the recreational ground, in the butcher’s car park, in the primary school, on the roads and even on junctions.”

A fleet of vehicles is understood to have arrived at about 5.30am on Saturday in the village. Video footage later showed men who took part in the protest disembarking from the back of the vehicles in Dover.

articles.title: U.A.E. warned Netanyahu of major Hamas operation days before Oct. 7 attack: Israeli newspaper
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was directly warned by the president of the United Arab Emirates that Hamas was planning a major offensive just days before the militant group led an attack on Oct.…

image.caption: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected calls for an official government inquiry into the events surrounding the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. On Tuesday, Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that he was directly warned by the U.A.E. that Hamas was planning a major offensive just days before

blocks.text: World·New

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was directly warned by the president of the United Arab Emirates that Hamas was planning a major offensive just days before the militant group led an attack on Oct. 7, 2023, according to an Israeli newspaper.
Haaretz says Netanyahu's office called report 'absolute lie'

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was directly warned by the president of the United Arab Emirates that Hamas was planning a major offensive just days before the militant group led an attack on Oct. 7, 2023 , according to an Israeli newspaper.
U.A.E. President Mohammed bin Zayed spoke with Netanyahu 10 days before the attack and said Yahya Sinwar, the leader of Hamas in Gaza at the time, was planning an operation, the Haaretz daily said.

Bin Zayed said it would lead to bloodshed and could destabilize the region and undermine the Abraham Accords, the normalization agreements between Israel and several Arab and Muslim-majority nations, the newspaper reported.

But Netanyahu "reacted with relative calm," according to Haaretz, which said he assured bin Zayed that Israel was prepared for any scenario and a possible attack was more likely to come from the occupied West Bank.
The attack led by Hamas militants on Oct. 7 killed some 1,200 people and took another 251 hostage, according to Israeli officials.
Haaretz reported Netanyahu's office called the report an "absolute lie" and said Netanyahu did not speak with the U.A.E. president "during the period in question and received no warning from him."

items: Israeli clearance of Gaza rubble could destroy evidence of 'atrocity crimes,' says UN expert
Israel prepared to remove Palestinians from Gaza if U.S. approves, defence minister says

blocks.text: Netanyahu has rejected calls for an official government inquiry into the events surrounding the Oct. 7 attack. His office did not respond to a request for comment.
The U.A.E.'s Foreign Ministry also did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Israel is holding national elections next month and Netanyahu's actions around the time of the Oct. 7 attack are a key issue in the campaign.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former top general seen as Netanyahu's main opponent in the election, accused the prime minister of ignoring dozens of warnings ahead of the attack.
"He is unfit," Eisenkot wrote on social media.
Another Netanyahu rival, Naftali Bennett, said, "Netanyahu bears personal and direct responsibility for the failure that led to the deaths of thousands of Israelis on his watch."
Israel's offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,650 Palestinians, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia vows to respond after Houthis attack cities and energy facilities
articles.summary: The Iran-backed Yemeni group's attacks have injured 73 people and caused fires at oil facilities, Saudi authorities say.

blocks.text: The spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, said the Houthi drone and missile attacks targeted civilian and economic sites in the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, and that women and children were among the injured.
An energy ministry statement cited an official source as saying that injuries were also reported after "several energy sector facilities and installations" were targeted.
The attacks "caused fires at several locations, leading to a temporary halt in some operations," they added.

Maliki described Houthi attacks as a "dangerous escalation that confirms the hostile and irresponsible approach of this terrorist militia" and said the Saudi-led coalition would "take all necessary operational measures to deter" the group.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea accused the Saudi military of carrying out more than 120 air strikes on the Yemeni provinces of Marib, al-Bayda, Hudaydah, Taiz and Jawf over the past three days, and of committing "grave crimes".
He said the Houthis had responded to this "brutal aggression" with "dozens of ballistic missiles and drones", which he claimed caused "significant damage".
A Saudi-led coalition of Arab states has backed Yemen's government against the Houthis in the country's devastating civil war for more than a decade.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

There has been heavy fighting on Yemen's south-western coast since Thursday, when the Houthis launched an offensive against Yemeni pro-government forces in a bid to take control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
The fighting has reportedly left more than 300 people dead and displaced 18,500.
The Red Sea has become crucial for oil shipments from Saudi Arabia during the US and Israel's war with Iran, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

articles.title: US real estate agent duct-taped and zip-tied to plane seat after ‘racial slurs’ is fired
articles.summary:
The man, also accused of homophobic slurs on American Airlines flight, faces assault and disorderly conduct charges

An Arizona…

blocks.text: An Arizona realty company says it is “no longer associated” with an agent who was recently arrested after alleged unruly behavior – including racist and homophobic slurs – on an airline flight led to his being zip-tied, duct-taped to his seat and arrested.

Layne Arthur Lundeen, 67, faces counts of disorderly conduct and second-degree assault in the case, according to Maryland court records filed after he was taken into custody at Baltimore’s airport on 3 September.

Two fellow passengers who helped detain Lundeen later gave an interview to ABC News which described how he acted belligerently and hurled “racial slurs” on an American Airlines flight that took off from Dallas, which drew widespread attention. And one of them provided a photograph of Lundeen restrained with duct tape and zip ties in a plane seat that went viral online.

That set the stage for Tucson’s Long Realty Company, where Lundeen listed himself as a vice-president, broker and realtor, to issue a statement on Monday on social media saying it had “ended its affiliation” with him.

“The individual is no longer associated with or authorized to represent Long Realty in any capacity,” the company’s statement said. “The conduct described in the reports is wholly inconsistent with the professionalism, integrity, compassion, and respect for others that Long Realty expects from those affiliated with the company.”

Lundeen on Tuesday did not immediately respond to a request for comment about Long Realty’s statement or what authorities are portraying as the latest high-profile case of misbehavior – often criminal – colloquially referred to as air rage.

American Airlines said in a statement issued to media outlets that flight 618 was traveling from Dallas Fort Worth international airport to Newark Liberty international airport on 3 September when there was a “disruptive” passenger about two hours into the trip.
The plane was diverted and made an emergency landing at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall airport at about 10.15pm, and the passenger was arrested there, officials said.
Court records showed Maryland transportation authority police arrested Lundeen at the airport that day and booked him with two misdemeanors. He was released on his own recognizance the next day.

Yet the matter did not end there for Lundeen. Another traveler on the diverted flight, former law enforcement officer Juan Mejia, spoke with ABC on 4 September and recounted how the man identified as Lundeen had “made derogatory remarks to the staff of American Airlines and other passengers – racial slurs, vulgar language, very offensive to the women” sitting in his vicinity.
The New York Post, citing police, reported that Lundeen also spouted anti-gay insults.
Mejia and a friend accompanying him, Richard Olenick, told ABC that they intervened when Lundeen made the situation physical.

“Juan immediately knew that action had to be taken,” Olenick said to ABC. “He got up right away and jumped in the seat right next to the passenger and began working on restraining him in order to keep the situation contained.”
Olenick also supplied photos of Lundeen bound to a window seat with duct tape and zip ties.
In short order, Lundeen’s links to Long Realty surfaced, and the company spent part of the Labor Day holiday on Monday announcing it had severed its relationship with him.

“We expect those associated with our company to uphold those values, and we have no tolerance for conduct that so clearly falls short of those expectations,” said the company’s statement, which did not name Lundeen. “Our focus remains on serving our clients and community in accordance with our values.
“Our thoughts are with the passengers, crew members and others affected by this incident.”
Lundeen as of Tuesday was tentatively scheduled to be in court in Glen Burnie, Maryland, on 19 October in connection with his arrest.

articles.title: New York City releases documents about air quality after 9/11
articles.summary: Officials assured the public the air was safe after the attacks, but the new documents suggest there were concerns.

blocks.text: New York City has released previously unseen documents raising concerns about air quality in Manhattan in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Tuesday.

The documents from 25 years ago suggest that officials had concerns about toxic air after the World Trade Center towers collapsed, while the public was being reassured the environment at the site, known as Ground Zero, was safe.
"People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air," Mamdani said at a news conference, surrounded by survivors.
The release resolves a lawsuit brought by advocacy group 9/11 Health Watch, which sued the city for the documents.
City officials found 68 boxes of the documents last year. Officials had previously said they did not have them.
"Administration after administration has ignored those calling for answers and clarity," he added, standing next to television host and 9/11 survivor advocate Jon Stewart. "We will do no such thing."
Thousands of people have experienced health effects like cancer from the terrorist attacks, including many who have died, after breathing in hazardous contaminants from the building collapses.
Mamdani said on Tuesday that he planned to release hundreds of thousands of pages of air quality reports through an online portal, timed with the 25th anniversary of the attacks.
He said City Hall will spend more than $34m (£25m) on the effort.
Mamdani said the documents show what the city "knew about the toxic air around Ground Zero, when they knew it, and how they acted to limit liability".
The mayor said the documents show asbestos was found "nearly everywhere" they tested. He said more documents will be released over the course of the next year.
The release comes after years of survivors advocating for more transparency from city officials.
Speaking at the news conference on Tuesday, Stewart said the documents show the city didn't recognize that the air that everyone was breathing in downtown Manhattan was toxic until October of 2001.
"So to be fair to them, they only buried that information for 25 years," he said sarcastically.

The documents include an October 2001 file known as the "Harding Memo", in which an aide warned former Deputy Mayor Robert Harding - serving under Mayor Rudy Giuliani - that the city could face as many as 35,000 legal claims for its response to the attacks.
The document states that the city could be sued because health advisories caused individuals "to return to the area too soon (causing toxic exposure or emotional harm)".

Days after the attack, city and federal officials - including the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) - declared that the air near the Twin Towers was safe, though research suggests people were breathing in toxic chemicals.
Christine Todd Whitman, the head of the EPA at the time, later apologised for this declaration, saying the agency "did the very best we could at the time with the knowledge we had".
Illnesses related to the dust and smoke from the collapse of the Twin Towers have claimed twice as many lives than the attacks themselves.
Elizabeth Cascio, a former New York Fire Department (FDNY) emergency medical technician, previously told the BBC that she suffered sinus issues and headaches after responding to the attacks.

"We all knew the air quality was not safe – it was very toxic in terms of how it felt," she said. "Initially, when I came off the bus and arrived at the Trade Center, you felt like you had to hold your breath. But there's only so long you can hold your breath. I could feel the particles coming into my nose and mouth and thought: 'This can't be good'."

articles.title: Four Renoir paintings worth millions stolen in French museum heist
articles.summary: It is the latest in a string of high-profile art thefts in Europe that has again put the security of museums and galleries in the spotlight.

blocks.text: What we know about the Renoir museum heist
ByMichael Sheils McNamee and Tiffany Wertheimer
Four paintings by the impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been stolen from a museum in the south of France.
Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on Tuesday morning but dropped two of the paintings in the institution's garden as they made their escape, local Mayor Bryan Masson said.
"Attacking the Renoir Museum is attacking a part of the history and heritage of Cagnes-sur-Mer," he said.

The paintings, each worth €9m (£7.7m; $10.4m), are the latest high-profile pieces to have been stolen this year following a string of heists in Europe - which have included four Renaissance paintings being stolen from a museum in Sicily just last month.
CCTV footage has captured the thieves entering the museum gardens by cutting through a fence before they cut through structures holding the paintings' frames in place, the local mayor said.
He added that two painting were "abandoned" in the gardens and have now been recovered.
The two paintings that are still missing are:

items: Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano (1910)
Jeune fille au puits (1886)

blocks.text: And the two pieces that were recovered are:

items: Portrait of Madame Pichon (1895)
Coco Lisant (1905)

blocks.text: "It's Renoir's, it is priceless, you cannot sell it like that," the mayor told reporters at the museum.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Jeune fille au puits and Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano are still missing

blocks.text: Image source, Musée Renoir
Jeune fille au puits and Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano are still missing

blocks.caption: Image caption, The thieves dropped Coco Lisant and Portrait of Madame Pichon when they fled - one was found hours later in the museum's garden

blocks.text: The thieves dropped Coco Lisant and Portrait of Madame Pichon when they fled - one was found hours later in the museum's garden
The museum's alarm went off at 05:48 local time (06:48 BST), and police were at the scene within five minutes, Masson explained, saying the thieves fled the scene upon hearing the security alarms.
Masson later told reporters that the thieves seemed to be "well-equipped" and "well-informed".
They were "wearing helmets, gloves, and combat gear" and carrying "an electric knife and hacksaw," Masson said.
Masson also confirmed that investigators had found two zip-up bags at the scene, which may have belonged to the suspects.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Police arrived at the scene within five minutes of the museum's alarm going off

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Police arrived at the scene within five minutes of the museum's alarm going off
The Renoir Museum is home to 12 of the famous painter's artworks.

Opened in 1960, it was Renoir's last home before his death in 1919, and also features many things that once belonged to him, including his easel and wheelchair, as well as photographs and personal letters.
The robbery has once again thrust the security of art in some of Europe's leading galleries and museums into the spotlight.
One of the most high-profile was in October last year, when a brazen heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris saw France's priceless crown jewels being stolen.
"Beyond Cagnes-sur-Mer, this incident should serve as a warning about the protection of our museums, which now face a new form of organised crime targeting works of art," Masson warned.
The mayor called on the French government to provide more financial support to local areas and museums to protect artwork from "increasingly organised and determined criminals".

articles.title: Teodoro hits China for rejecting South China Sea arbitral award: Of course, you lost
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Gilberto "Gibo" Teodoro lashed out at China's massive claims in the South China Sea after he was handed an unsigned note while speaking before a defense and security forum in Seoul,…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 9:30pm

Defense Secretary Gilberto "Gibo" Teodoro lashed out at China's massive claims in the South China Sea after he was handed an unsigned note while speaking before a defense and security forum in Seoul, South Korea.
According to JP Soriano's report on "24 Oras," the note said China didn't recognize the arbitral award that nullified its historical claims in the South China Sea.
"Of course. Because you lost,” Teodoro said in a panel discussion at the Seoul Defense Dialog as he responded to the pro-China points raised in the note. It was not clear where it came from.
Teodoro indicated that China should have joined the forum hosted by South Korea.

“I think this is from China… You should have joined the... and may I read it? ‘China's position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent, and firm.’ They have no position!” Teodoro said.

“'The so-called award is illegal, null and void.' So say you. ‘And has no binding force.’ Because you don't want to be subjected to UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea)," he added.
Teodoro called the gesture from China rude, asking how one could deal with such behavior. He added that it was also disrespectful to the host.

“How do you expect to deal with it civilly? I ask you the question: Is this the right paper to pose to me when I am being asked a question on the floor? And how will you treat this kind of behavior?” Teodoro said.
GMA News has reached out to the Chinese Embassy in the Philippines for a response.

In the midst of continued harassment from China in the West Philippine Sea, Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) officials have expressed concern over the submarine cables, pipelines, and other infrastructure in the sea.

“The risks are expanding from traditional natural disasters and piracy to gray-zone tactics, state-sponsored cyberattacks, physical sabotage, and the hybrid realities of geopolitical friction,” said DFA Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim without naming a country.
Meanwhile, Justice Undersecretary Dennis Chan also questioned what legal remedies the Philippines has.

“In such a case, why can't the coastal state, like the Philippines for that matter, prosecute these foreign offenders directly? This situation highlights the gap and inadequacy of existing laws to deal with these modern problems,” Chan said. –Jean Mangaluz/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Remulla: Negotiations underway with Bato dela Rosa’s ‘protectors’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said negotiations were underway with purported protectors of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa. “We know where he is, but there are negotiations now…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said negotiations were underway with purported protectors of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa.
“We know where he is, but there are negotiations now with his protectors and I think we’ll get to him soon,” Remulla said in an interview on One News’ Storycon program on Tuesday.
“I cannot really talk at length about it, but he’s being protected by very powerful people.”
The Inquirer sought comment from dela Rosa’s office and legal counsel, Israelito Torreon, but both have yet to respond as of this writing.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) and the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) have been searching for dela Rosa since last May to serve an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant for his arrest over his alleged involvement in former President Rodrigo Duterte’s bloody drug war.
Dela Rosa was last seen leaving the Senate premises and supposedly getting off in Makati City in the early hours of May 14, shortly after a shooting incident in the chamber.
Remulla justified the supposed negotiations, saying, “We don’t want casualties involved. That’s number one. They have to surrender peacefully.”
“And we will use all the levers of the government to get him out of his hiding, using all the economic and military levers that we have in order to force him out,” he stressed.
The DILG chief further noted that the PNP was working to take custody of a total of 117 firearms registered to dela Rosa.
At least 26 firearms had been surrendered by the senator’s camp since last June.
This came after the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office revoked dela Rosa’s firearms license and gun registrations as part of the government’s bid to locate him. /mcm

articles.title: Highlights: Day 23 of Sara Duterte impeachment trial | Sept. 8, 2026
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Day 23 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Tuesday centered on two major procedural developments: a looming decision on the voting threshold needed for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Day 23 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Tuesday centered on two major procedural developments: a looming decision on the voting threshold needed for conviction, and the formal pivot to Article II, the unexplained-wealth charge.

Presiding officer and Senator-judge Francis Escudero announced that amici curiae (friends of the court) will be heard on September 16, with oral arguments of the parties scheduled for September 23, when the Senate is expected to vote on whether to retain the 24-member voting base for the trial.

Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo had raised the issue, citing concerns about senators who may be unable to physically participate in the final conviction or acquittal vote, given that Sens. Loren Legarda is on sick leave, Ronald dela Rosa is in hiding, and Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada are detained in connection with plunder cases.

On the evidentiary front, the prosecution told the court it would skip the remaining 15 of 27 witnesses for Article I and instead reserved the right to call Duterte herself to the witness stand to address all articles of impeachment.
Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan announced the move, saying the prosecution had already presented 10 witnesses and stipulated two others, making the remaining Article I witnesses unnecessary.

Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison immediately objected, invoking the Constitutional prohibition against compelling an accused to testify against herself, calling the prosecution’s possible move an attempt at impermissible testimonial compulsion.
With Article I witnesses concluded, the court set September 14 as the start date for Article II proceedings on Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.

Rep. Chel Diokno, lead prosecutor for Article II, told the court on Tuesday that more than 1,800 documents, including bank and insurance records produced under court-issued subpoenas, are set for marking on September 9 and 10, with trial proceedings suspended on those days so both sides can participate.

The Senate impeachment court separately gave Duterte’s lawyers 15 days to respond to the prosecution’s Request for Admission covering 104 items related to Article II, including bank records the prosecution seeks to confirm belong to the vice president.

Escudero also announced the broader trial schedule running through November, with whole-day trial sessions scheduled for October 1, 2 and October 5 to 15, and a break from October 16 to November 8 to make way for 2027 national budget hearings and plenary debates. The revised calendar was approved in an all-senators caucus, according to Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri. /dp

articles.title: UK retailers aim to create 100,000 jobs for young people out of work
articles.summary:
In partnership with DWP, firms such as John Lewis and M&S plan to offer 18- to 24-year-olds placements of two to four weeks

UK retailers aim to create up to 100,000 jobs for young people…

blocks.text: UK retailers aim to create up to 100,000 jobs for young people not in employment, education or training (Neet) over the next three years by giving them a first step on the ladder into work.

In partnership with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), more than 40 retailers, including Marks & Spencer, Pets at Home, Asda and the John Lewis Partnership, will offer Neets aged 18-24 placements of two to four weeks to gain “the skills and confidence needed to take their first step into work”.

The move comes after the former health secretary Alan Milburn warned in a recent report that the 1 million Neets in the UK could rise to 1.25 million over the next five years unless ministers intervened.

Milburn, who is leading a review into Britain’s crisis in youth worklessness, welcomed the retailers’ initiative, saying too many young people were stuck in a vicious cycle of “no experience, no job”, leaving them shut out of employment opportunities.
He said: “Six in 10 young people who are Neet have never had a job. Unless we can increase work opportunities, Britain’s Neet crisis will get worse not better.”
Other employers signed up to the scheme include Tesco, New Look, Wickes, Currys and Greggs.
The prime minister, Andy Burnham, said: “Opportunities like these can make all the difference, helping young people gain the confidence, skills and connections they need to get started in work.”
The scheme, known as Opening Shift, follows the appointment earlier this year of the former M&S chief executive, Marc Bolland, to head a taskforce to tackle the growing youth unemployment crisis.

Bolland, who led the retail chain from 2010 to 2016, has secured the support of retailers for the work placement scheme amid warnings that the country risks a “lost generation” without urgent intervention.

Participants will continue to receive universal credit throughout their placement, mainly because of the logistical barriers claimants face when accepting short-term jobs that mean quitting and then rejoining the welfare programme.
The programme was developed with retailers through the British Retail Consortium and the DWP and has 11,305 placements already pledged.

Bolland, who is also a senior non-executive director at the DWP, is understood to have been chosen for the role thanks to his involvement with the charity Movement to Work, which had already helped more than 200,000 unemployed young people find jobs.
He said: “My work as founder and chairman of Movement to Work showed me first-hand what’s possible when business and government work together to open doors for young people.
after newsletter promotion

“Today’s announcement takes that further, creating thousands more opportunities for young people to build a future in one of Britain’s biggest industries and I’d encourage every retailer to look at what more they can offer.”

Each participant will be guaranteed an interview at the end of their placement, which will vary from 16 to 35 hours each week. Retailers will offer each recruit a “buddy” to help them navigate the new role, with the aim of moving as many recruits as possible into a job should one be available, Bolland added.
The DWP said it would use jobcentres to allow Neets to access the scheme.
Helen Dickinson, the chief executive of the BRC, said: “Retail is uniquely placed to make a difference on the Neets crisis, given the industry’s scale and reach touching every corner of the country.
“Work experience is a first step, and with the right conditions for businesses to invest and create new entry-level jobs, employers across the economy can help tackle the Neet crisis.”

articles.title: From conflict to elections: Bangsamoro's path to self-rule in BARMM
articles.summary: For generations, the story of the Bangsamoro has been shaped by a struggle for self-determination, marked by armed conflict, displacement, peace negotiations, and repeated attempts to establish…

blocks.text: For generations, the story of the Bangsamoro has been shaped by a struggle for self-determination, marked by armed conflict, displacement, peace negotiations, and repeated attempts to establish meaningful autonomy in the southern Philippines.
On September 14, 2026, that long history will enter a new chapter.

The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is set to hold its first parliamentary elections, allowing voters to choose the representatives who will form the region’s first elected parliament.
The election marks a major step in the transition from an interim government through the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) to an elected regional administration.
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. described it as the “fruition of an entire peace process that began in 1968, then the Tripoli Agreement, and then the BARMM.”
The elections are also a crucial test of whether the decades of peace efforts can be translated into a stable and democratic self-government.
However, the significance of the election cannot be understood without looking back at the history that led to the establishment of the BARMM.
Decades of struggle

The Bangsamoro homeland has a long history that existed even before the Philippines became an independent country. Muslim communities in Mindanao and the Sulu Archipelago developed their own societies, traditions, systems of leadership, and Islamic identity. They also resisted foreign domination during the Spanish and American periods.
Conflicts and disagreements between the government and various Moro groups continued for decades.

Events such as the Jabidah incident in 1968 contributed to the growth of the Moro struggle for self-determination. The Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), and later the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), became important groups in the history of this struggle.
A significant step toward autonomy came in 1989 with the establishment of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) through Republic Act (RA) 6734.

The ARMM was later strengthened and expanded through RA 9054 in 2001. These laws provided an autonomous government for Muslim-majority areas of Mindanao within the framework of the Philippine Constitution.

On September 2, 1996, the government and the MNLF formally signed a peace agreement that ended a quarter of a century of fratricidal war in Mindanao. It was concluded after four years of tough negotiations held in Libya, Jakarta, Indonesia, and Mindanao.

At the same time, peace talks were ongoing from 1997 to 1999 with the MILF, a breakaway faction of the MNLF. In March 2000, then-president Joseph Estrada declared an all-out war against the group, which prompted it to withdraw from the negotiations.
The talks were formally resumed in 2001 under then-president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo.
Here’s a timeline of the negotiations with the MILF that paved the way to the establishment of the autonomous region:
March 2001: The government and the MILF signed the Agreement on the General Framework for the Resumption of Peace Talks.

June 2001: The Tripoli Agreement on Peace was signed, with Libya and Malaysia playing important facilitating roles. The agreement centered on security, ancestral domain, and rehabilitation and development.
May 2002: The Joint Communiqué establishing the Ad Hoc Joint Action Group was signed as a form of cooperation against criminal groups in areas associated with the MILF.

2004: Malaysia became more involved with the creation of the International Monitoring Team, which helped oversee the ceasefire and contributed to confidence-building between the government and the MILF.

July 2008: The government and the MILF negotiated a Memorandum of Agreement on Ancestral Domain (MOA-AD) in July 2008. It was supposed to be signed on August 5, 2008, in Kuala Lumpur. However, the Supreme Court issued a temporary restraining order on August 4, 2008, preventing the signing. Violence subsequently erupted involving MILF breakaway elements, which displaced thousands.
July 2009: The government and the MILF agreed to mechanisms for suspending military operations.
June 2010: The government and MILF signed the Declaration of Continuity for the Peace Negotiations ahead of the takeover of the Aquino administration.
October 2012: The government and the MILF signed the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro, which set the foundation for creating a new autonomous political entity called the Bangsamoro.
March 2014: The government and the MILF signed the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, described as the culmination of years of negotiations between the two sides.

July 2018: Republic Act 11054, or the Organic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (Bangsamoro Organic Law or BOL), was signed by then President Rodrigo Duterte. The law created the legal framework for the BARMM, replacing the ARMM. It aims to provide the Bangsamoro with a greater degree of self-government while still remaining part of the Philippines.
January 2019: The BOL was ratified through a plebiscite. A second plebiscite was held in February 2019. These enabled the establishment of the BARMM.

The BARMM currently consists of the provinces of Basilan (excluding Isabela City), Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, and Tawi-Tawi; the cities of Cotabato, Marawi, and Lamitan; and eight municipalities in North Cotabato that voted for inclusion in 2019.
Sulu, although originally included in BARMM after the 2019 plebiscite, was excluded following a 2024 Supreme Court ruling because the province voted against ratifying the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
Commemorating the seventh year of the BARMM's establishment in January 2026, Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua said the region is solid in moving toward a single direction.

“Seven years ago, BARMM was born not out of comfort but from conviction. It grows from a long and difficult history in which we endured conflict, displacement, and neglect. Yet, we never surrender our faith, our dignity, and our right to decide our own future,” said Macacua.

“BARMM today stands as a symbol of unity. We came from different paths and perspectives, yet we learned that no institution can stand, and no progress can last, if we work against one another,” he added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Martin Romualdez deemed flight risk by DILG despite health issues
articles.summary: “Martin Romualdez is a flight risk. Dalawa ang kanyang private jet, tatlo ang kanyang helicopter, tatlo ang kanyang yacht. He is a flight risk. Kaya gagawin na namin ang lahat ahead of time para…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 9:09pm
The Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) is treating former speaker Martin Romualdez as a flight risk despite having several health conditions.
According to Jun Veneracion's report on "24 Oras," Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that Romualdez had enough means to escape.

“Martin Romualdez is a flight risk. Dalawa ang kanyang private jet, tatlo ang kanyang helicopter, tatlo ang kanyang yacht. He is a flight risk. Kaya gagawin na namin ang lahat ahead of time para preventive ang kanyang containment dito,” Remulla said.
(Marton Romualdez is a flight risk. He had two private jets, three helicopters, and three yachts. He is a flight risk, so we will do everything ahead of time to make his containment here preventive.)

Romualdez, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, Romualdez's personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Serenio; and Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation have been charged with plunder before the Sandiganbayan.
The charges are in connection with the alleged P7.4 billion in kickbacks from flood control and other government projects from 2022 to 2025.
The court in issuing the warrant of arrest on Romualdez and his co-accused also issued a hold-departure order.
Co is in Europe and is the subject of a request for a red notice from the Interpol. Serenio and Guevarra are also at large.
A lawyer fo Romualdez has said that he will face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess, his camp said Monday.
He has repeatedly denied allegations that he benefited from kickbacks tied to the flood control projects.

“We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” he added.
Romualdez's camp has since asked the Sandiganbayan to grant him continued hospital confinement, citing a medical history concerning his cardiovascular health and brain condition.
In another report on "24 Oras" by Maki Pulido, Romualdez’s doctors have reported that moving him may pose a risk to him, considering his medical conditions.
The former speaker has complained of chest pains, and he has coronary artery disease and psychological anxiety, his camp said.
Doctors from the Philippine National Police have already assessed the former speaker and came up with the same conclusion as his doctors, Remulla said.
Remulla stressed that he received no orders from President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to treat Romualdez differently, even if Romualdez is Marcos’ cousin.
The DILG chief said that Romualdez being his fraternity brother also had no bearing.

“I told him, ‘Brother, I hope you understand why I’m doing this. It’s nothing personal,’ and he said, ‘It’s okay, I understand’,” Remulla said in a mix of English and Filipino. –Jean Mangaluz/NB, GMA News

articles.title: BSW and AfD – a political love-hate relationship in Germany
articles.summary: The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) could help the Alternative for Germany (AfD) into power in Saxony-Anhalt. It is riddled with infighting

image.caption: AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund (top) could become head of government in Saxony-Anhalt with the support of the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW)Image: Karina Hessland-Wissel/Jan Huebner/IMAGO

blocks.text: Following the election in Saxony-Anhalt, there is no clear governing coalition because the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) with its 44% share of the vote has fallen just short of securing an absolute majority. That means the formation of a new government in one of Germany's 16 federal states is more difficult than ever. This is also partly due to the success that the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), which was founded only in 2024, has managed to achieve. Wagenknecht, a trained economist, was a longtime member of the socialist Left Party, formerly a communist who over time has distanced herself further from her political roots. Her party does not conform to traditional labels. Many people can no longer relate much to labels like "left" or "right," she says.
From the very beginning, Wagenknecht also showed no reluctance to engage with the AfD. Her long-held credo has been that the party includes people who are treated unfairly if labeled as Nazis.
What next after far-right AfD win in regional election?

Now, Sahra Wagenknecht and her followers are working towards seeking common ground with the AfD and can even imagine helping the party's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund into the role of state premier by abstaining from the vote. Wagenknecht mentioned this scenario before the September 6 election.
Both AfD and BSW oppose 'uncontrolled migration'

A few days before the vote, Sahra Wagenknecht spoke on TV broadcaster ntv about overlapping policy preferences of BSW and AfD voters: "These are people who have similar concerns: They want controlled migration, they do not want this uncontrolled migration and they want above all that politics is again conducted in their interests, that their lives are the focus."

However, there is also a significant degree of agreement on issues other than German immigration policy: both parties call for an end to German arms deliveries to Ukraine, which has been attacked by Russia in violation of international law. Or they claim that freedom of speech no longer exists in Germany.

Whether the BSW will actually team up with the AfD remains completely open. AfD lead candidate Siegmund emphasized even before the election that he intended to govern only with an absolute majority of his own.

blocks.caption: Sahra Wagenknecht is no longer the chairwoman of the BSW party, but still its most prominent representativeImage: dts Nachrichtenagentur/IMAGO

blocks.text: When the BSW was founded in January 2024, it had a spectacular start: Formed as a splinter party from the socialist Left, the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) was swiftly elected to the European Parliament and in the same year received double-digit results in three state parliament elections. In the eastern German states of Brandenburg and Thuringia, the party entered straight into government coalitions. That would also have been possible in Saxony, but coalition negotiations with the CDU and the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) failed.

The BSW favors a tough approach to refugees. It opposes any form of military support, whether for Ukraine or for Israel. The BSW advocates for an end to German weapons deliveries to Ukraine, which was attacked by Russia in breach of international law.

The party's leader, economist Sahra Wagenknecht, who grew up in communist East Germany, aligned her new political home beyond traditional classifications. She repeatedly states that many people can no longer relate to labels like "left" or "right" wing.
Wagenknecht has also had no reservations about contact with the AfD from the beginning. As early as 2023, she stated that some people within the party were being labeled Nazis unfairly.
Far left? Far right? What is Germany's BSW?
From rising star to struggling party

However, the BSW in Saxony-Anhalt has ruled out a classic coalition. Following elections in Brandenburg and Thuringia in 2024, the branches in those states went against the stated will of their founder and joined governments alongside established parties. The permanent conflict between the federal leadership of the party and its state branches led to the breakdown of the coalition with the Social Democrats in Brandenburg, starting in 2025.

In Thuringia, led by a coalition of the CDU, SPD and BSW, most of the BSW lawmakers declared that they were leaving the party two days before the election in Saxony-Anhalt. However, they wanted to remain a part of the CDU-led state government. "We have not been elected to tolerate flirts with right-wing radicals," is how Finance Minister Katja Wolf explained this decision, referring to the rapprochement with the AfD initiated by Wagenknecht.

The BSW's success in Saxony-Anhalt and accompanying key role in the formation of the government has given the party, at least for the moment, a largely unexpected significance. This is because during the Bundestag federal election of 2025 the BSW narrowly failed to reach the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament and, also due to its many internal conflicts, it seemed to have little credibility among the population.

Furthermore, its figurehead Sahra Wagenknecht has stepped back from the leadership of her party and is no longer running for its chairmanship. She continues to exert her influence in the background, though, and is a drawcard at BSW rallies, especially during election campaigns.
Boost for upcoming state elections?

Following their successful entry into Saxony-Anhalt's parliament, which according to pre-election polls was by no means guaranteed, Wagenknecht responded confidently: "The BSW's comeback has begun," she told German news agency dpa. How sustainable this upswing is will be revealed on September 20, when parliamentary elections will be held in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and the city-state of Berlin.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: House OKs bill setting barangay, SK execs’ term to five years
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A bill that proposes a fixed five-year term for barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials, with a maximum of two successive terms through reelection for the same…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A bill that proposes a fixed five-year term for barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials, with a maximum of two successive terms through reelection for the same position, has been approved by the House of Representatives.
During the session on Tuesday, House Bill (HB) No. 10971 was approved after 211 lawmakers voted in the affirmative, with only 13 voting in the negative and one abstention.
If enacted, HB No. 10971 will amend Section 1 of Republic Act No. 12232, changing the term of office of barangay officials from the current four years to five years.

Furthermore, the bill effectively suspends the 2026 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE), as the measure states that the date of the next BSKE will be on the second Monday of November 2028, and every five years thereafter.
For current officials HB No. 10971 placed a transitory provision stating that incumbents should be considered as having completed due to the extension of their terms by two years.
Meanwhile, incumbent officials who are in their consecutive term in the same position will be allowed to run for the same post in the November 2028 BKSE.
Kabataan party-list Rep. Renee Co, one of the lawmakers who voted against the bill, said that HB No. 10971 said that suspending the BSKE again is a violation of the 1987 Constitution.

“This representation believes that we will be cheated again with this bill. This is a clear violation of the Constitution and the decision of the Supreme Court in Macalintal v. Comelec. We push for the suspension of the BSKE from 2026 to 2028 and extending the term of sitting officials for two years without providing sufficient basis,” she said.

“The Court said that postponing the elections needs to have a ‘compelling governmental interest’ like protecting suffrage or a true emergency — not merely administrative convenience o seeking for ‘continuity.’ It has not been a year since we passed a law that extends the term of BSK officials to 4 years, we will extend their term again for another year?” she asked.

This is not the first time that the House pushed for a measure extending the term of barangay and SK officials. During the 19th Congress, former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez and other ranking lawmakers proposed setting a fixed term of six years for barangay and SK officials, to ensure continuity of projects and to shield them from politicking.
Romualdez was referring to HB No. 10747, or the proposed Act Setting the Term of Office of Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Officials to Six Years.

According to the Speaker, he and House lawmakers decided to set a fixed six-year term for barangay officials to do away with confusion brought by recent term extensions, poll suspensions, and other laws.
However, Romualdez’s bill does not allow officials to serve more than two successive terms in office.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has already suspended the 2022 BSKE, upon the prodding of lawmakers from the House and the Senate to use the funds for pandemic recovery instead.
However, the Supreme Court in June 2023 declared the law unconstitutional, ordering the BSKE to proceed last October 2023. /das

articles.title: Marcos vows to sustain PH education push after PISA gains
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday vowed to sustain his administration’s education push after the country achieved its strongest performance yet in the Programme for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday vowed to sustain his administration’s education push after the country achieved its strongest performance yet in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).
The PISA 2025 results showed that the country’s mean scores rose to 373 in science, 371 in mathematics and 367 in reading—up 17, 16 and 20 points, respectively, from its 2022 scores.
The Philippines outperformed 14 countries in science, 16 in mathematics and 18 in reading, according to the report.
In a video statement, Marcos welcomed the development and credited the gains to the collective efforts of teachers, parents, and communities.

“Isn’t that good news?” Once again, this proves how capable our students are—that they are hardworking and serious about their studies, and how good our teachers are, as long as they are properly supported,” he said.
“So let us not stop. Here in our administration, we will not stop. We will further strengthen our serious efforts to address these challenges,” he added.

Citing the PISA report, Marcos highlighted that the Philippines is among the few education systems improving across all domains and is considered one of the fastest-improving education systems globally, with the strongest long-term improvement in reading among participating systems.
He said the government was only beginning to implement programs and other initiatives aimed at improving the lives of students and teachers.

“We will continue all of this. We will continue everything we are doing. We are just getting started. We have only begun building classrooms, providing internet access, computers and school supplies, and printing books,” he said.
“We can see that when we unite in improving the lives of our students, we can truly feel the very positive results,” he added.
PISA is an international study that measures the reading, mathematics and science knowledge and skills of 15-year-olds.

The assessment is administered by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and involves 15-year-old students from more than 90 countries and economies, typically near the end of compulsory basic education. /mcm

articles.title: SC upholds graft conviction of ex-Siquijor town mayor, 4 others
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has upheld the conviction of former Mayor Orville Fua of Lazi town, Siquijor province, and four others for graft in connection with the irregular procurement…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has upheld the conviction of former Mayor Orville Fua of Lazi town, Siquijor province, and four others for graft in connection with the irregular procurement of fertilizers worth more than P4.9 million in 2004.

The high tribunal’s Second Division, in a decision promulgated on Jan. 22, but made public only on Tuesday, affirmed the 2023 ruling of the Sandiganbayan that found Fua and former Lazi officials Sue Castillon, Natalio Jumawan, Jr., Rose Marie Tomogsoc, guilty beyond reasonable doubt of violating Sec. 3(e) of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
Castillon was the municipal engineer and a bids and awards committee (BAC) member, Jumawan was the municipal treasurer and also a BAC member, and Tomogsoc was the municipal accountant.
Also convicted of the same offense was Merlyn Lu of Mangopina Trading, Inc., the winning bidder in the fertilizer procurement.
They were meted a prison term of up to 10 years and were perpetually disqualified from holding public office.
The Supreme Court said that the transaction failed to undergo the mandatory pre-procurement conference as the cost of the fertilizers exceeded the threshold under bidding rules.

Fua and the other Lazi officials also did not comply with other requirements under Republic Act No. 9184, or the Government Procurement Reform Act, such as the holding of proper advertisement or invitation, notice of award and performance security bond.

The high court also ruled that Mangopina was not eligible to supply the fertilizers as it had a bad record in government transactions, failing to pay for the renewal of mayor’s permit or license in 2003 and 2004.
It was also running on a license that expired in 2022, it noted.

“In other words, Mangopina was granted unjustified benefit despite its sheer lack of qualifications and patent multiple disqualifications,” read part of the 18-page decision penned by Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier. /das

articles.title: Legarda pushes merit, accountability reforms for 2.25M gov’t workers
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda urges greater investment in the skills of the more than 2.25 million personnel keeping government services running across the country and stronger systems…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda urges greater investment in the skills of the more than 2.25 million personnel keeping government services running across the country and stronger systems that reward performance, measure results, and hold public institutions accountable.

As the country marks the 126th Philippine Civil Service Anniversary this September, Legarda said recognition for government workers should be matched by policies that give them better opportunities to improve their skills and make it easier for the competent and ethical among them to perform their jobs well.

“When an employee’s work is good, the people feel it. Transactions are faster, service is better, the answers of agencies are clearer, and public funds are better used. If the standards we expect from public servants are high, the government should also be serious about giving them better opportunities,” Legarda said in a statement issued on Tuesday.

Citing a Civil Service Commission report, she said there are 2,256,693 career and non-career government personnel as of June 2026. This year’s anniversary carries the theme “Bawat Kawani, Lingkod Bayani: Puso, Dangal, at Galing Para sa Bayan.”

Legarda, who chairs the Senate Committee on Civil Service, Government Reorganization and Professional Regulation, has filed measures addressing professional development, merit-based performance, government accountability, and access to public information.
Among these are the following:

items: Senate Bill No. 2099, or the proposed Government Employees Free Master’s Degree Tuition Act, which seeks to provide free tuition in state universities and colleges for government employees pursuing master’s degrees
Senate Bill No. 513, or the proposed Bagong Dugong Lingkod Bayan Act, which seeks to establish a National Public Service College tasked with developing competent and ethical government leaders

blocks.text: “Many workers want to study and expand their capabilities, but there are expenses involved in graduate education. If the knowledge that they will get will be used for making better policies and rendering better services, it’s only right that the government should invest in their education,” Legarda said.
Legarda is also pushing for reforms in how government performance is evaluated through the following measures:

items: Senate Bill No. 1850, which seeks to establish and institutionalize a performance measurement system that promotes meritocracy in government
Senate Bill No. 515, or the proposed National Results-Based Governance Act, which seeks to strengthen monitoring, evaluation, and the use of evidence across government programs and projects

blocks.text: “Performance evaluation should be meaningful. If the work is good, it should be recognized. If a program isn’t working, it should immediately be identified and corrected, and not continue to be funded because it’s the way it’s always been done. Public funds should follow programs that actually work,” Legarda said.
She stressed that measuring performance also requires access to reliable information and stronger safeguards against corruption.
To this end, Legarda has filed the following measures:

items: Senate Bill No. 523, or the proposed Tapat na Paglilingkod Act, which seeks to institutionalize a national anti-corruption mainstreaming agenda and strengthen integrity and accountability mechanisms throughout government
Senate Bill No. 304, or the proposed Open Government Data Act, which seeks to require the proactive and regular publication of policy- and operations-relevant government data

blocks.text: Legarda said these measures reflect the kind of civil service reform she intends to pursue as committee chair, with professional development matched by merit, measurable performance, transparency, and accountability.

“No matter how good a policy is, if the system of implementation is weak, the people won’t feel it. So it’s important to strengthen our workers and the institutions where they serve so that every law, program, and funding allocated by the government will go to real services that will benefit the people,” Legarda said. /atm

articles.title: Sandro Marcos takes on bigger role as House majority leader
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — When Sandro Marcos entered the House of Representatives in 2022, he was a first-term congressman learning the workings of the chamber. Three years later, he took on a much…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — When Sandro Marcos entered the House of Representatives in 2022, he was a first-term congressman learning the workings of the chamber. Three years later, he took on a much bigger role as House majority leader, putting him at the center of the House’s legislative agenda.
Marcos was unanimously elected majority leader at the opening of the 20th Congress on July 28, 2025.

The position made him the spokesman of the House majority and placed him in charge of directing deliberations on the floor. He also concurrently chairs the Committee on Rules, which handles matters involving the House rules, its calendar of bills, and the preparation of its Order of Business and Calendar of Business.

In practical terms, the role puts Marcos in a position to help determine how the House moves through its legislative agenda. Rather than being limited to introducing his own bills, he works with the chamber’s leadership and members of the majority bloc to facilitate the passage and discussion of measures.
He also has to keep track of legislation moving through the House and help ensure that bills scheduled for floor deliberation are ready for consideration.

That responsibility became apparent early in the 20th Congress. By January 2026, Marcos reported that 7,030 bills and 645 resolutions had already been filed during the first 22 session days of the new Congress. Of these, 86 measures had been approved, including 12 measures endorsed by the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council, or LEDAC. Marcos has repeatedly emphasized the importance of moving priority measures through the legislative process.

In February, he pointed to the progress of eight LEDAC priority bills that had reached advanced committee stages. He described the committee process as important for building consensus, refining policies, and making sure measures were ready before reaching the floor.

The majority leader’s role was also visible during the House’s special session in June 2026. During the proceedings, Marcos noted that the chamber had already approved all measures identified in the presidential proclamation that called for the special session.
By the end of the first regular session in July, the House had approved 26 of the 52 priority measures identified by LEDAC.

Marcos said the chamber would work on the remaining measures during the second regular session, while also stressing the importance of making laws easier for the public to access and benefit from. The numbers provide one measure of the House’s output, but Marcos’ position is ultimately about more than legislation moving from one stage to another.

As majority leader, he is part of the leadership responsible for keeping the chamber’s business moving, coordinating with lawmakers, and helping translate the administration’s legislative priorities into measures that can be debated and voted on.

The position is also a significant step from where Marcos began. When he first entered Congress, he was elected senior deputy majority leader in the 19th Congress. The role placed him in the Committee on Rules and gave him an early leadership position despite being a rookie lawmaker.
Now, as majority leader, Marcos has moved from learning the House’s legislative machinery to helping operate it.

With the 20th Congress still underway, his leadership will increasingly be judged by how effectively he helps the chamber manage its priorities, navigate debates, and move legislation forward. For Marcos, the job is no longer simply about representing one district. It is about helping steer the work of the entire House.

articles.title: New Hampshire voters head to polls in race crucial to Democrats’ Senate hopes
articles.summary:
Centrist Chris Pappas faces progressive primary challenger Karishma Manzur while Republicans eye chance to flip seat

New Hampshire voters head to the polls Tuesday for primaries that will…

blocks.text: New Hampshire voters head to the polls Tuesday for primaries that will set up a closely watched Senate contest – a vulnerable open seat Democrats must defend if they are to have any shot at reclaiming the upper chamber.

The race opened when Jeanne Shaheen, 79, the state’s three‑term incumbent Democratic senator, announced her retirement. Congressman Chris Pappas, who represents New Hampshire’s first district, is seeking the nomination and enters the final stretch with a clear financial edge: more than $4m cash on hand, according to his latest filings. But his main challenger, Dr Karishma Manzur – a scientist and progressive activist with no experience holding public office – has gained ground.

If he wins the primary, Pappas, 46, is likely to face the Donald Trump-endorsed former senator John E Sununu, who is seeking a return to the seat he once held and is part of a political dynasty that includes his father and brother, both former governors.

“This is the kind of place where you can’t just run a bunch of TV ads and expect to win,” Pappas told the Guardian. “You’ve got to meet people where they are. We’re finding support in corners you might not expect – including from people who voted for Trump last time but are open to a conversation about moving the country forward.”

A popular centrist, Pappas has served in the House since 2019 and has crossed the aisle at various points. He calls himself “battle‑tested” and has consolidated establishment backing, earning endorsements from leading Democratic lawmakers and former vice‑president Kamala Harris. His family’s name also carries weight in New Hampshire: the Pappases own the Puritan Backroom, the century‑old Manchester restaurant famed for allegedly inventing the chicken tender and long embedded in the state’s retail‑politics circuit.

Sununu, 61, is the clear frontrunner in the GOP primary, though he faces Scott Brown – another former senator who represented Massachusetts, later moved to New Hampshire, and served as US ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during Donald Trump’s first term.

The president threw his support behind Sununu earlier this year despite the former lawmaker’s past criticism of the president, including a 2024 op‑ed in which Sununu called Trump a “loser” and backed Nikki Haley in the Republican presidential primary.

On the trail, Sununu has tried to show daylight between himself and the administration, criticizing Trump’s tariff policy, urging Congress to rein in executive power, and questioning the decision to launch military action in Iran. He told New Hampshire Public Radio it was “a tactical mistake” to go to war “without having a plan for protecting the strait of Hormuz”. That posture may matter in a state where Trump’s approval rating sits at 38%.
Sununu and Brown did not respond to the Guardian’s interview requests.

Kristen Cianci, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee (RNC), said that Sununu was a “strong candidate” who was “well positioned to beat out Pappas” in a general election. “While Democrats have been consumed by infighting, Republicans have been laser-focused on real issues like affordability and security,” she added in a statement.

Some Democrats worry New Hampshire could become a sleeper risk – a state where Republicans control the legislature but haven’t won a Senate race since 2010, when Kelly Ayotte, the now-governor, captured a seat. Pappas insists he’s not taking anything for granted, and is running like he’s “10 votes behind” at all times – especially in a midterm cycle where progressive challengers have scored surprise primary wins across the country. This, however, hasn’t fazed Pappas who says he is running as a “New Hampshire Democrat” who knows his state.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Former senator John E Sununu, who is seeking the GOP nomination for his old seat, takes a selfie with a supporter in Berlin, New Hampshire on 22 August. Photograph: Holly Ramer/AP

blocks.text: But Manzur, who supports Medicare for All and higher taxes on mega‑corporations and the ultra‑wealthy, has repeatedly highlighted the money Pappas has received from donors aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. She casts him as milquetoast and ineffective. “I was tired of choosing between the lesser of two evils and still seeing so much pain and suffering right here in my state,” she said, calling both Pappas and Sununu “corporate politicians”.
“One has a ‘D’ after their name. One has an ‘R’ after their name … neither of them have been able to address the real needs of the people,” Manzur added.

Pappas, for his part, has long backed US aid to Israel but told the Guardian that Benjamin Netanyahu was “not a trustworthy ally of the US” and said he hoped the Israeli prime minister is ousted in the country’s October election. Pappas noted he has rejected corporate Pac money in this race but did not directly address his support from pro‑Israel donors, instead pointing to a “broad‑based effort” of individual contributors that have supported his Senate bid.
Pappas says he would support the Democratic nominee if he loses. “We need a big tent and new voices in the party to win tough elections,” he said at last week’s Democratic debate.

Manzur declined to make the same commitment. “I’m focused on winning,” she told the Guardian. “I’m not going to get into these discussions – they’re intentionally distracting from the people’s movement.”

Further down the ballot, the Democratic primary for Pappas’s House seat has drawn eight candidates, with Stefany Shaheen – daughter of the outgoing senator – and Maura Sullivan, a former Obama administration official, leading the field. The district, long purple, has been reliably blue since 2017. Republicans now see it as flippable, and Trump has endorsed Anthony DiLorenzo, a businessman who owns several car dealerships, in the GOP race.

articles.title: After years of commuting, students in 3 Gitxsan communities have a high school of their own
articles.summary: A new high school serving three Gitxsan communities in northwestern B.C. has officially opened, giving students the chance to complete grades 8 to 12 closer to home in a school rooted in Gitxsan…

image.caption: Community leaders from across three Gitxsan nations celebrated the opening of Gitksen West Secondary School, which will serve 170 students. (Gitksen West Secondary School/Facebook)

blocks.text: British Columbia

A new high school serving three Gitxsan communities in northwestern B.C. has officially opened, giving students the chance to complete grades 8 to 12 closer to home in a school rooted in Gitxsan culture, language and community.
School serves students from Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla, who previously travelled 60 km to Hazelton
Students from three Gitxsan communities in northwestern B.C. no longer have to travel to Hazelton for high school, following the opening of a new secondary school in Gitwangak.
The Gitksen West Secondary School will serve the communities of Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla, located between 98 to 117 kilometres northeast of Terrace, B.C.
The aim is to give students the opportunity for secondary education in a culturally enriched learning environment rooted in Gitxsan culture, language and community, leaders say.
On Thursday, hereditary chiefs, matriarchs, band councils, elders and other community members from the three communities celebrated the school’s opening at Gitwangak.
Indigenous Services Canada provided about $39 million for the design and construction, as well as program delivery for the first year of operations.

items: More stories from Northern B.C.

blocks.text: “Reclaiming education holds profound significance for our people, especially given the history of residential schools,” said Gitwangak Chief Chasity Daniels, who is also president of the Gitksen West Secondary School Society.
The project has been more than a decade in the making, she added.
“Today, we are bringing education home and creating opportunities for our children on our own terms.”
The school is locally governed by a school board representing the three communities, said Indigenous Services Canada in a news release.
"We see a day when we have our youth succeed in our communities with dogwood certificates and not leaving certificates,” said Gitsegukla Chief Coun. Annie Howard.

In B.C., a leaving certificate, otherwise known as a School Completion Certificate or Evergreen Certificate, is for students who finish their school program without meeting standard graduation requirements.

items: Land-based curriculum expands to kindergarten at Yellowknife school

blocks.text: Previously a 60 kilometre commute
The new school has the capacity for up to 170 students from nearby communities from grades 8 to 12. It includes 12 classrooms, a library, kitchen, gymnasium and other facilities.
Previously, students had to commute 60 kilometres away to Hazelton, B.C., to attend high school.
"This is the start of a new era where we empower our flowers to bloom in a world that can benefit from Indigenous knowledge and ways of being,” said Gitanyow Chief Bryan Williams.
“I look forward to seeing Gitksen scholars contributing to our future."

items: Kitselas First Nation celebrates opening of new community centre

blocks.text: “I am excited to be a part of the process, to demonstrate that First Nations culture has academic value, looking to develop a collaborative relationship not just with students, but with parents and community,” said Principal Elmer Moody in a video on the school’s Facebook page.
“I am looking forward to the demonstration that our culture has a place in education.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Catherine Garrett is a CBC News reporter based in Terrace, B.C., covering the province's northwest region. Born in Ontario and raised on Haida Gwaii, she has previously worked in Vancouver, Prince George, B.C., and Grande Prairie, Alta. She has received multiple awards for her work, including a Canadian Online Publishing Award. You can contact her at catherine.garrett@cbc.ca.
