articles.title: Afghanistan's women: A national soccer team without a home
articles.summary: The Afghan women's national football team has finally been officially recognized by FIFA. Now the players want to make history both on and off the field.

image.caption: The Girl Power Summer Camps are a game changer for Afghanistan's women's teamImage: Irving Villegas/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: On the football pitches of Bundesliga club Wolfsburg, the Afghanistan women's national team is training and doing exactly what is strictly forbidden in their home country: playing football.

In the first session of the day, the coaches' main focus is helping the players get to know each other better and have fun. That's because, as of April of this year, these young women are now officially allowed to play football as the Afghan national team.
FIFA, the world's football federation, has amended its regulations, allowing Afghan women to once again represent their country in official international matches and FIFA competitions.

"This was a huge victory for us, a wonderful moment, and one of the moments we're most proud of. Because once again, the women of our country have made history and brought about change," Khalida Popal told DW. The former captain and founder of the organization Girl Power has been a pioneer for women's football in her country.
Karimi: 'I'm incredibly proud'
Since the Taliban took power in 2021, the players and Popal have fought for the recognition that has now become a reality.
"I'm incredibly proud that we can now officially play as a national team," said midfielder Maryam Karimi.
For Karimi, who has been living in Portugal since fleeing Afghanistan, FIFA's decision is more than just a formality.
"I hope that one day we'll be able to play in Afghanistan again with this team."

blocks.caption: Almut Schult (fourth from the left) coaching the Afghanistan women's teamImage: Irving Villegas/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Until then, however, Afghanistan remains a national team without a home.
"We'll probably be one of the first national teams in history that has no home and no country in which to play," said Popal. "We'll compete from exile and represent our country."
Today, the players are scattered across the world. Many have traveled from England, Italy, Portugal or Germany, but some have also found refuge in Australia.
"We come from different countries and can't play together regularly. But when I see the players, they're incredibly united. They keep going and push each other forward,” said Karimi.
Gaining More Visibility Through Football

The 39-year-old Popal wants to use her experience to help the players and advance their athletic development. She wants the national team to be known not only for what was taken from them, but also for what it achieves on the field.

"The first goal, of course, is to build a strong team that performs well on the field," said Popal. "Because the better we play, the better we can represent our country, and the more visible we'll become."

But that is precisely where the biggest challenge currently lies. In Afghanistan itself, a regular system for women's football cannot be established at this time. As long as the Taliban are in power, women are not allowed to play sports.

So there is nowhere for young talent to be nurtured; there is no funding and no support from the country the players represent. This is because the Afghan Football Federation — unlike FIFA — does not recognize the women's team. For the time being, therefore, the team's future must be built outside the country.

"We have no federation and no country where talent can develop," said Popal. That is why the team relies heavily on the Afghan diaspora. There, the team is looking for players who may never have played for a club in Afghanistan, but who could represent their parents' country in the future.
Popal: 'The Taliban are erasing women from society'

To organize football camps like these, the women rely on outside support. The summer 2026 camp was made possible by an invitation from Volkswagen and Wolfsburg, but Popal and her organization still have a lot of work ahead of them.

Giving players who have fled Afghanistan a place back in international football is one part of the challenge, but so is creating structures and a foundation on which Afghan women's football can be built.
"It will be a team that stands up to the Taliban. Because the Taliban are erasing women from society,” said Popal.
"We will play football to stand up for the women of our country. When the players take the field, they're also playing for those women in Afghanistan who aren't allowed to."

blocks.caption: Almuth Schult & Khalida Popal talking at Girl Power Summer CampImage: Irving Villegas/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Just like the former captain, the other young women on the team feel the same way. Midfielder Karimi wants to use football to draw more attention to her friends and all the women in her homeland.
"I can make my voice heard through the way I play football," Karimi said. "I can make my voice heard from the field."
Popal: "These girls are our future”

Despite a long battle for the human rights taken away from women by the Taliban, Popal keeps pushing because she wants to make sure that the women wearing the national team's jersey today are not the last generation to do so.

"I believe that Afghanistan won't stay this way forever. These dark days will pass. These girls will be the next coaches of the Afghan women's national team, the next directors of football academies, the next president, or the next ministers of our country," said Popal.
"And that is exactly why we are investing in these girls: because they are the future.”
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Fourteen men go on trial in Paris over deadliest small-boat Channel crossing
articles.summary:
Sinking of inflatable dinghy in 2021 resulted in 31 people dead or missing, including a seven-year-old child

Fourteen men will go on trial in Paris on Tuesday over the deaths of at least 31…

blocks.text: Fourteen men will go on trial in Paris on Tuesday over the deaths of at least 31 people in the worst mass drowning from a small-boat crossing in the Channel on record.
The accused men, alleged to be linked to people-smuggling networks, face charges including manslaughter and facilitating illegal immigration as part of an organised criminal group.
Twenty-seven people were confirmed dead when their inflatable dinghy sank in the early hours of 24 November 2021. Four people remain unaccounted for.

The victims were mostly Iraqi Kurds, but also included people who were Afghan, Ethiopian, Iranian, Somali, Vietnamese and Egyptian. The youngest known victim was a seven-year-old girl. The confirmed dead also included 15 men, seven women and two teenagers.
A team on a French fishing boat near British waters off Calais had raised the alarm when they saw several lifeless bodies floating in the water.

According to testimony from the two survivors, the flimsy boat which had attempted to cross one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes – between the northern French coast and Kent in southern England – began to deflate and take on water after several hours at sea.
Passengers fell overboard and drowned one after another, despite making about a dozen desperate calls for help to French and British rescue services. Only two men survived the tragedy.

Investigators allege that Afghan and Iraqi-Kurdish smuggling networks ⁠organised the migrants’ passage to Britain from camps near Grande-Synthe and Calais in northern France. The defendants face charges including involuntary manslaughter, facilitating illegal immigration as part of ⁠an organised gang and criminal conspiracy.
Two of them, including an Afghan man, are the subject of arrest warrants and will be tried in absentia.

Among the defendants are alleged organisers, transporters and logistics coordinators connected to the ​smuggling groups. Prosecutors argue their actions helped create the conditions that led to the disaster, even if some were not physically present when the boat launched.
Prosecutors have accused the defendants of helping launch a “substandard small boat, uncertified, unfit for navigation on the open sea, overcrowded and lacking appropriate lifejackets”.

Liability has also been extended to those accused of transporting, housing or accompanying the victims, actions that formed part of a “chain of successive events” leading to the tragedy, according to investigators.
The defendants have denied being smugglers and disputed their responsibility, or have presented themselves as people who were seeking to make the journey themselves.
However, phone records and location tracking placed several of them near the departure site and linked them to organising crossings to Britain.
For the people onboard the sinking boat, despite several distress calls, it was nearly 12 hours after the first pleas for help before the dinghy was finally found by the French fishing vessel.

A separate investigation is ongoing in France into seven French military personnel – five members at a maritime rescue coordination centre, and two sailors onboard a patrol vessel – who have been under investigation since 2023 for failing to help a person in danger. They deny the allegations.

The UK’s Cranston inquiry, in its report released in February, found that systemic failings, missed opportunities and inadequate resourcing undermined the UK’s maritime search and rescue response on the night of the disaster. HM Coastguard was placed in an “intolerable position”, it said, with chronic staff shortages and limited operational capacity contributing directly to the failure to rescue people in the water.
It found the deaths would have been “avoidable” if British and French authorities had acted sooner to rescue those onboard.
Families ​of some of the victims will travel from Erbil in Iraqi Kurdistan to attend part of the trial, their lawyers said.
“Justice must hold accountable everyone who played a role in this tragedy,” the lawyers, Matthieu Chirez, Thomas Ricard and Camille Renouard, said in a statement.
Agence France-Presse and Reuters contributed to this report

articles.title: Laguna de Bay rises to 12.73 meters, above critical mark
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The water level at Laguna de Bay continued to rise above its critical high-water mark, reaching 12.73 meters as of 1 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 8, the Laguna Lake Development Authority…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The water level at Laguna de Bay continued to rise above its critical high-water mark, reaching 12.73 meters as of 1 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 8, the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) said.
In its 1:15 p.m. advisory, the LLDA attributed the rising lake level to persistent heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon and a low-pressure area.

The latest reading surpassed the 12.68-meter level recorded at 9 a.m. on Monday, Sept. 7.The LLDA classifies 10.50 meters as the lake’s critical low-water level and 12.50 meters as its critical high-water level.
The agency advised residents living along the shores of Laguna de Bay to “prepare for potential flooding and strictly adhere to local evacuation protocols if continuous rainfall persists.”

At least 29 lakeshore barangays remained flooded, affecting communities in the towns of San Pedro, Biñan, Santa Rosa, Los Baños, Bay, Calamba, Santa Cruz, Pakil and Paete, according to various news reports.
Laguna de Bay has served as a natural catch basin for water from the watersheds in Laguna and Rizal provinces, as well as parts of Metro Manila. /das

articles.title: Metal detectors, CCTV to be installed as security measure in Albay school
articles.summary: LEGAZPI CITY — Local government units (LGUs) in the Bicol Region are strengthening safety in public schools through additional security equipment, improved emergency communication systems, and skills…

blocks.text: LEGAZPI CITY — Local government units (LGUs) in the Bicol Region are strengthening safety in public schools through additional security equipment, improved emergency communication systems, and skills training for students and community responders.

In an interview, Sto. Domingo, Albay Mayor Nomar Banda said they plan to expand closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in schools and establish a centralized public address system that can be used to relay emergency alerts.

He said they will talk with the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office to study the system and explore the possibility of connecting it with the Philippine National Police for coordination during emergencies.
The LGU also plans to conduct martial arts and self-defense training during the summer for students, parents and village watchers (tanod).
Banda said the training will provide participants with basic skills that can help them respond to emergencies.

Before the budget is approved for the provision of walk-through metal detectors in schools, Banda said he also donated a walk-through metal detector to Sto. Domingo National High School and plans to provide another unit to San Fernando National High School within the month.
He said the equipment will ensure that persons entering the premises are checked.
In another interview, San Fernando National High School Principal Serapion Gongona Jr. said they require all students to carry identification (ID) cards, and use a school-purchased metal detector.
“Those without an ID are not allowed to enter,” Gongona said.
He said the school prohibits sharp objects and firearms, noting that potential security threats may come, not only from outside the school, but also from within the student community.
Shaila Jane Torre, a teacher at San Fernando National High School, said strengthening school safety measures is important in helping teachers protect learners.
“As teachers, our priority is the safety of our learners. It is very difficult for a teacher, especially when handling 30 to 50 students in a classroom, so we need to be prepared,” Torre said. /apl

articles.title: Man reported missing found safe in Itogon
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — A man who had been reported missing was found safe near a creek in Itogon, Benguet, on Tuesday, Sept. 8, after police, barangay officials, and relatives searched areas near his home.…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — A man who had been reported missing was found safe near a creek in Itogon, Benguet, on Tuesday, Sept. 8, after police, barangay officials, and relatives searched areas near his home.
The search team scoured nearby pathways and the vicinity of a creek, where they eventually found the man sitting about 100 meters from his home.
The man was reportedly suffering from Alzheimer’s disease, which may have caused him to become disoriented and wander away from his residence.
Police and barangay personnel immediately assessed his condition and found minor scratches on his forehead and both thighs.
They administered first aid before carefully assisting him uphill to a safer location, where his family could attend to him and arrange further medical evaluation when needed. /mcm

articles.title: German police arrest suspect in power grid sabotage case
articles.summary: Investigators say the suspect used homemade rockets and conductive wire to target high-voltage lines in three German states, apparently as part of a campaign against fossil fuels.

image.caption: Police mounted a search after two short circuits in one of the incidents in BrandenburgImage: Frank Hammerschmidt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German police on Tuesday said they had arrested a 48-year-old man suspected of carrying out a series of sabotage attacks on the country's electricity network.
The suspect was reportedly spotted near the Weisweiler power station, close to Aachen in western Germany, after being sought by authorities for several days.
How were the attacks carried out?

Investigators suspect the man of trying to cause short circuits at several locations in the states of North Rhine-Westphalia, Brandenburg and Saxony over the past week, using homemade rockets to fire thin conductive wire across high-voltage power lines.
The method appears to have worked in at least two cases.
In Bergheim, west of Cologne, several units at a power station were put out of operation for several days.
At a substation near the Jänschwalde power station in Brandenburg, more than 20 homemade rockets were allegedly used to fire conductive material onto power lines, causing two short circuits.
However, neither incident resulted in a power outage.
Sabotage fears hit Germany's power grid
Last week, armed police located and raided a truck thought to have been used in the attacks.
What was the suspected motive?
Investigators have linked a series of letters claiming responsibility for the attacks to the 48-year-old suspect from Gevelsberg, in the southern Ruhr region.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the letters contained information that could only have been known to the perpetrator.
"The knowledge revealed in these letters is clearly knowledge belonging to the perpetrator," Dobrindt said.
He described the attacks as apparent "climate terrorism" carried out by a lone offender.
In the letters, the suspected attacker reportedly justified targeting the electricity network as part of a campaign against fossil fuels.
"Generating electricity from fossil fuels is a crime," one of the letters said.

Lignite is still mined and used for electricity generation in all three states where the suspected attacks took place. The burning of lignite releases massive amounts of carbon dioxide into the air, a major factor in climate breakdown.

articles.title: PISA flags classroom disciplinary climate as area for improvement in PH
articles.summary: The classroom disciplinary climate in Philippine schools remains an area requiring attention, with Filipino learners reporting disruptions due to noise, lack of attention and difficulty working…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 6:52pm

The classroom disciplinary climate in Philippine schools remains an area requiring attention, with Filipino learners reporting disruptions due to noise, lack of attention and difficulty working during Science lessons, according to the Department of Education’s presentation of the 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results.
DepEd’s PISA 2025 presentation identified disciplinary climate as one of the areas that needs improvement, even as learners also reported strong levels of support from their teachers.
Among Filipino learners surveyed, 79% said noise and disorder disrupted at least some Science lessons.
Meanwhile, 75% reported that students do not listen to what the teacher says, while 65% said students cannot work well in at least some lessons.
PISA’s disciplinary-climate measure looks at the extent to which disruptions in the classroom can interfere with students’ opportunities to learn.
The OECD has previously described the measure as covering factors such as noise and disorder, students listening to teachers, and students’ ability to concentrate on academic tasks.
Strong teacher support
The findings on classroom discipline were disclosed alongside relatively strong reports of teacher support from Filipino learners.
According to the DepEd presentation, 86% of Filipino learners said teachers show interest in every student’s learning.
Another 88% said teachers continue teaching until students understand, while 87% said teachers provide extra help when students need it.
This suggests that while learners generally report receiving support from their teachers, the broader classroom environment remains a challenge.
The findings also come as the Philippines posted its highest PISA scores since joining the assessment in 2018, with mean scores of 367 in Reading, 371 in Mathematics and 373 in Science in 2025.
Digital devices add to classroom challenge
Digital-device distraction was another issue highlighted in the PISA 2025 presentation.

About 75% of Filipino learners said their peers were often distracted by digital devices during some Science classes. More than 80% of learners attended schools with policies governing digital-device use.
The finding comes as DepEd has been increasing its focus on digital access and technology in schools.

During the House Committee on Appropriations hearing on Monday, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said digital familiarity had also been a concern in previous PISA assessments, with some Filipino learners reportedly encountering a computer mouse for the first time during the assessment.
Why classroom climate matters
The classroom environment matters because disruptions can reduce the time and attention available for learning.

The OECD has found in previous PISA assessments that students who reported a better disciplinary climate tended to perform better in Reading, even after accounting for students’ and schools’ socioeconomic profiles.

The PISA 2025 findings point to a challenge beyond simply improving test scores: the Philippines also needs to strengthen the classroom environment in which those learning gains are expected to happen.
At the same time, the strong teacher-support figures suggest that the issue is not simply about teacher engagement, but also about the broader conditions affecting classroom learning. — BAP, GMA News

blocks.text: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is holding its first parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026, after being postponed at least four times: first in May 2022, then in May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026.

The historic polls are seen as a pivotal moment in the decades-long peace process in a region that was mired in conflict and socioeconomic and political challenges. The upcoming elections are also a test for the Bangsamoro transition and the institutions and systems established in the last seven years.

articles.title: Prevent outside influence in Bangsamoro polls, groups urge Marcos
articles.summary: Civil society also urges the Moro Islamic Liberation Front 'not to fan the flames of division'

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Civil society groups urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday, September 8, to prevent external actors from attempting to influence the outcome of the Bangsamoro parliamentary polls and undermine the autonomy the region fought hard for.

Duyog Bangsamoro, a coalition comprised of regional and national civic organizations, urged the national government to continue supporting the peace process “regardless of which parties win the elections.”

“They have to make sure that this election turns out to be peaceful and credible,” Josua Mata, secretary general of labor group Sentro ng mga Nagkakaisa at Progresibong Manggagawa, said in a press briefing Tuesday.
Duyog Bangsamoro said there is a “persistent perception” in the region that Malacañang has been meddling with the affairs of the regional government.
This started when Malacañang made “irregular appointments” to the transition government, the group said, which deepened cracks within the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).

“We call on the AFP and PNP personnel assigned to the region to observe the highest level of professionalism and reject influence from any actor that would deprive the Bangsamoro people of a genuine exercise of their autonomy,” their statement read.
The historic election is a milestone in the peace process between the Philippine government and the MILF.

But other things have yet to be done, such as decommissioning former combatants and the implementation of transitional justice. (READ: Transitional justice for Bangsamoro should be a ‘national project,’ say peace advocates)
The call for peaceful and credible elections followed MILF’s recent move to dismiss a number of its commanders and strip Abdulraof Macacua of his position as the organization’s military chief.

Macacua is the Bangsamoro interim chief minister, running in the 3rd parliamentary district of Maguindanao del Norte. Macacua has refused to run under the banner of United Bangsamoro Justice Party, the MILF’s official regional parliamentary political party.

This move manifested a long-running conflict inside the MILF. However this affects the election outcome, Amina Rasul, president of the Philippine Center for Islam and Democracy, said that MILF’s decision is their prerogative.

“It’s within their right,” Rasul said on Tuesday. “In truth, we don’t know the rationale for that. We have to accept the decision and just make sure that everything is going to proceed as peacefully as possible.”
To the MILF, the coalition said: Don’t fan the flames of division, continue to engage in debates, and instruct the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces to “stand down.”

Over 2.3 million voters are expected to participate in the September 14 parliamentary elections. The Bangsamoro region is electing political party and district representatives. The elected parliament will eventually choose one member to become the chief minister. – Rappler.com
Quotes translated to English for brevity.

articles.title: Hungary orders 10 Russian diplomats to leave
articles.summary: Budapest says the expulsions are necessary to protect security and sovereignty after years of comparatively close ties between Hungary and Russia.

image.caption: Hungary said the embassy staff's activities were incompatible with their diplomatic statusImage: Aled Betts/cc-by/Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Hungary has ordered 10 members of Russia's diplomatic mission to leave the country over activities it said were incompatible with their diplomatic status, Foreign Minister Anita Orban said on Tuesday.
The move marks a significant step by Budapest against Moscow, with Orban saying it was intended to protect Hungary's "security and sovereignty."
Why is Hungary expelling the diplomats?
Orban said a Hungarian Foreign Ministry official had informed the Russian ambassador that the 10 individuals had engaged in activities deemed "unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention."
She did not specify what the individuals were accused of doing.
Hungary's authorities had made the assessment before the government called on them to leave, Orban said.
"This decision protects Hungary's security and sovereignty," she wrote.
Does this mean a break with Russia?
Orban stressed that Hungary was not severing diplomatic relations with Moscow.
"It does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia," she said, adding that Budapest intended to maintain "the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules."
Orban has served as Hungary's foreign minister and deputy prime minister since May, following the change of government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar.
The expulsion is nevertheless a notable deterioration in relations with Moscow, particularly given Hungary's previously close relationship with Russia under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban.

articles.title: Iran-backed Houthis attack Saudi oil facilities, injuring dozens
articles.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the…

image.caption: Storage tanks are seen at the North Jeddah bulk plant, an Aramco oil facility, in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, in this 2021 file photo. The Iran-backed Houthis said Aramco facilities were among those attacked Tuesday. (Amir Nabil/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle ‌East war.
Attacks on Saudi facilities threaten to worsen the global economic impact resulting from Iran war

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in the south of U.S. ally Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle ‌East war.

The Houthis, who control most of Yemen's populated areas, including the capital, said they had launched a broad operation deep into Saudi territory. They used drones and missiles to strike a Saudi airbase in the southern city of Khamis Mushait, and targets belonging to Saudi Arabia's state oil company in nearby Abha, Najran and Jazan, a major Red Sea port.

Saudi authorities described blazes at the sites and said women and children were among the 73 ​people hurt. The reports of such large numbers of wounded suggested the attacks were among the biggest ​carried out against Saudi Arabia since the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran in February.

Confirmed images of the aftermath of the attacks were not immediately available. The Houthis released pictures of an explosion of what they said were trucks from Saudi Arabia ​they had struck at the border in another area.
Houthi attacks on southwestern Saudi Arabia have the potential to worsen the war's global economic impact by disrupting Middle East energy supplies beyond the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

After a month of calm in August, fighting in the Gulf has resumed, with ⁠Iran and the U.S. exchanging fire, sending ⁠global oil prices back up to levels unseen since July. Brent crude prices were up more than ‌two per cent on Tuesday, above $99 US a barrel.

The ⁠fighting has caused global shortages of crude oil and, more acutely, the fuels that are produced by refining it. Diesel fuel in the United States is now at a record average retail price of more than $5.90 a gallon less than two months before midterm elections that could threaten the hold of Donald Trump's Republicans on one or both chambers of U.S. Congress.
Test of wills

Saudi Arabia has led an Arab coalition battling against the Houthis in Yemen for more than a decade. That war had calmed in recent years, but a ceasefire there has broken down, with the Houthis threatening shipping at the mouth of the Red Sea.

"The coalition ⁠will take all necessary operational measures to deter this terrorist militia and resolutely confronts its hostile approach," Col. Turki al-Malki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, said in a statement on X.
Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree accused Riyadh of having escalated the war by launching airstrikes on Yemen, and said the Houthis would respond.
The war in the Gulf has turned into a test of wills ‌between the U.S. and Iran, with each side hoping that economic pressure from competing blockades will force the other to yield.

Washington is trying to increase the flow of oil to world markets by guiding ships through the Strait of Hormuz at the mouth of the Gulf, while cutting off Iran's exports with a blockade just beyond it.

Tehran has announced new measures to seal off the strait, saying it will soon unveil details of a "maritime exclusion zone" that will extend from the ​perimeter of the U.S. blockade, through the strait and into the Gulf itself.
The U.S. fired at Iranian tankers over the weekend in retaliation for Iranian fire at American warships. Iran said it had used new, more capable ballistic missiles to attack.

"In ⁠recent days, Washington has received a clear warning from Iran’s new missiles," Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council said on X. "Economic warfare will be met by a ⁠maritime exclusion zone across the Persian Gulf to the blockade perimeter. The operational posture toward U.S. warships and bases has been fundamentally recalibrated."
Thousands on the move in Yemen

Despite U.S. barrages that have degraded Iran's ⁠conventional forces and ⁠punished its already ailing economy, Iran still possesses missiles and drones ​that can threaten oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz and have been used to attack U.S. military bases scattered throughout the region.
About one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural ​gas shipments passed through the strait before the war.

items: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Aramco oil facility in Saudi Arabia
War disrupts Irving Oil’s longtime Saudi crude supply

blocks.text: The flare-up between the Saudis and Houthis has displaced about 18,500 people in Taiz and Hodeida in southwestern Yemen, further pressuring communities in southern Taiz and the West Coast, according to the International Organization for Migration.

"Families are arriving with nothing: no shelter, no food, no way to know if it's safe to go back," said Abdusattor Esoev, IOM chief of mission for Yemen. "Many of these are people who have already been displaced once, twice, even four times before."

Yemen's civil war began in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and much of northern Yemen and forced the government into exile. A Saudi-led coalition intervened the following year to try to restore the government to power.
The civil war has killed at least 150,000 people, according to UN estimates, and at times pushed the country to the brink of famine.
With files from The Associated Press

articles.title: Oral arguments possible on VP Sara subpoena --impeachment court spox
articles.summary: Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol on Tuesday said oral arguments may be conducted if the House prosecution panel requests a subpoena to compel Vice President Sara Duterte to testify in her…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 6:38pm

Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol on Tuesday said oral arguments may be conducted if the House prosecution panel requests a subpoena to compel Vice President Sara Duterte to testify in her own impeachment trial.
This comes as private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan announced that the prosecution intends to call Duterte to the witness stand to confirm her allegation of innocence.
Kapunan, however, said that they are not asking the Senate impeachment court for a subpoena for the Vice President "at this time."
Tongol said the prosecution and the defense have opposing views on the matter, with the latter invoking the Vice President’s right against self-incrimination.

He also recalled that when the prosecution requested to subpoena the bank and tax records of Duterte, her husband Manases Carpio, and the businesses linked to them, the impeachment court decided to conduct oral arguments on the matter.

“Mukhang kung ‘yun po, dokumento lang, ito po ay medyo mas higher right of a person. Under the Bill of Rights po ‘yan, na right against self-incrimination ang kinukwestyon dito,” Tongol explained in a press conference.

(If that was just for a document, this one’s a bit more important as we're talking about the rights of a person. The right against self-incrimination under the Bill of Rights is being questioned here.)
“So kaya po mukhang mas importante ito at magkakaroon ng ganong prosesong oral arguments when the time comes that they request for the subpoena to be issued,” he added.
(So this seems more important and there will be such a process of oral arguments when the time comes that the prosecution requests for the subpoena to be issued.)
Tongol was also asked if Duterte could skip the trial if a subpoena is issued, and if she does, would she be cited in contempt even if she is the respondent.

“Well, that is within the realm of possibility sa multiverse of madness. Kasama ‘yan. So puwedeng mangyari ‘yun. However, siyempre, ang bawat aksyon ng isang tao merong kaukulang consequence. So ‘yung consequence na ‘yun, we will just cross the bridge when we get there, if ever that happens,” the court spokesperson answered.

(Well, that is within the realm of possibility in the multiverse of madness. That is included. So it can happen. However, of course, every action of a person has its corresponding consequence. As to that consequence, we will just cross the bridge when we get there, if ever that happens.)
Tongol admitted that it would be easier if Duterte just voluntarily attended her own trial, just like what former Chief Justice Renato Corona did to his.
Regardless, he stressed that doing so is totally the Vice President’s prerogative.

“Just like Chief Justice Corona, he was not called to the witness stand by the prosecutors then. He just volunteered. And as the defense counsel of CJ Corona then was saying against their advice to attend the trial, he insisted on attending the trial. So it is totally the respondent's prerogative if she wants to be a witness,” he said.
If ever Duterte decides to attend her impeachment trial, Tongol also said that people should have learned the lesson from what happened during the impeachment trial of Corona in 2012.

“Maraming nagsasabi na ‘yun ‘yung nakasama kay Chief Justice Corona, ‘yung hindi siya natanong. And seemingly, according to some people, nag-walk out siya on the impeachment proceedings. So I'm sure nobody will make the same mistake anymore, whether any witness ‘yan or even the respondent,” he said.

(Many people were saying it became worse for Chief Justice Corona when he did not take any questions. And seemingly, according to some people, he walked out on the impeachment proceedings. So I'm sure nobody will make the same mistake anymore, whether that’s for any witness or even the respondent.) —LDF, GMA News

Most of the cases were recorded in the barangays of Cararayan, Carolina and Concepcion Pequeña.
The Sangguniang Panlungsod approved the declaration following a recommendation from the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council amid the continuing rise in dengue cases.

Mayor Leni Robredo ordered the intensification of cleanup and search-and-destroy operations, particularly in areas identified as potential breeding grounds for mosquitoes, as part of efforts to contain the outbreak.
Robredo said the Naga City General Hospital had reached full bed capacity because of the influx of dengue patients.
The city government was considering using Super Health Centers as additional facilities for patients who needed to be admitted, she said. /apl

articles.title: Marcos welcomes Norway, South Korea ambassadors
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has welcomed the new ambassadors of Norway and the Republic of Korea to the Philippines during separate ceremonies at Malacañan Palace. Marcos on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has welcomed the new ambassadors of Norway and the Republic of Korea to the Philippines during separate ceremonies at Malacañan Palace.

Marcos on Tuesday first received the credentials of His Excellency Kristian Netland, ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary of the Kingdom of Norway. He underscored the “warm and very productive” relations between the two countries and expressed optimism about exploring new areas of cooperation.
“I think that there are many, many areas that we can continue to pursue and new areas that we can explore and develop,” Marcos told Netland.

“We are happy to count Norway as a friend of the Philippines, and we look forward to all that we will do to strengthen that relationship and to make deeper the engagements between our two countries,” he added.
Netland said the Philippines and Norway have enjoyed many decades of friendship “founded on trust, mutual respect, and a shared commitment to peace, democracy, and international cooperation.”
“Norwegian companies have been present in the Philippines for decades, contributing with expertise, technology, and jobs,” Netland said.

“As both our countries pursue sustainable growth and the green transition, I believe there are substantial opportunities to expand cooperation and create new partnerships that benefit our peoples,” he added.

Marcos also received His Excellency Lee Dong-gy as the new ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary of the Republic of Korea. He presented his letters of credence to Marcos in a separate ceremony.
In his brief remarks, Marcos expressed confidence that the Strategic Partnership between the two countries would be further enhanced during Lee’s tenure.

“As we know, the relations between our two countries have been very, very strong and very, very close for many, many years… I look forward to the work that we will do here together in the time you have here in Manila and in the Philippines as Ambassador,” Marcos said.
Lee said the Philippines and South Korea share a longstanding friendship built on “mutual respect, shared values, and close people-to-people ties.”
He added that the partnership between the two nations has continued to expand across the areas of politics, economy, defense and security, law enforcement, and culture.
Moreover, Lee conveyed South Korea’s full support for the Asean Chairmanship of the Philippines and reaffirmed South Korea’s continued engagement with the regional bloc.

“As ambassador, I will devote my utmost efforts to further strengthening this important relationship and to expanding our cooperation in ways that will bring tangible benefits to both our peoples,” he said.
Marcos held separate closed-door meetings with Netland and Lee at the Study Room. /mcm

articles.title: At least two people dead after Russian strikes on Kyiv
articles.summary: Air raid alerts and sounds of explosions rang out in Ukraine's capital as Russian forces launched drone strikes early on Tuesday.

blocks.text: At least two people have been killed after Russia resumed airstrikes on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv early on Tuesday, officials said.
The attack came after both countries agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days while US Donald Trump's top envoys visited Moscow and Kyiv.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday he expected the war to continue into the winter, following talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - their first visit to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion.
Air raid alerts warned civilians to seek shelter as Russian forces launched drone strikes on Kyiv early on Tuesday, authorities said.
A series of explosions across Ukraine's capital overnight killed two people and injured ten others, the city's state emergency service said on Telegram.
Residential buildings were hit, according to authorities, including a five-storey apartment block in the Solomianskyi district, while vehicles caught fire in the Podilskyi district.
People sought shelter inside a metro station in Kyiv during the overnight missile attack, something that is routine for residents protecting themselves during the ongoing war.
In Russia, buildings were struck in the city of Saratov during a Ukrainian drone attack, its regional governor Roman Busargin said on Telegram early Tuesday.
The talks with Trump's top envoys on Sunday in Ukraine, which lasted several hours behind closed doors, finished without any major breakthroughs.

Zelensky told reporters they had agreed that officials from Ukraine, Europe and America would meet in the near future to continue discussions. He also called for a trilateral meeting with Russia and the US.
According to a BBC Verify analysis, Kyiv is suffering more daily air raid alerts than at any time since Russia's invasion in 2022.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 23: Prosecution wants VP on the stand
articles.summary: The 23rd day of Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial kicked off with private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan informing the impeachment court that they would not present additional witnesses for…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 6:12pm

The 23rd day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial kicked off with private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan informing the impeachment court that they would not present additional witnesses for Article 2, which alleges the misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds, unless the Vice President herself takes the witness stand.

Kapunan cited that based on the testimony of the four witnesses presented by the prosecution on alleged confidential fund misuse, it is only the Vice President who has the proper knowledge to explain the disbursement of the said funds that were allocated to the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education, when it was under Duterte's helm.

“All of these pawns and castles and horses and bishops point to only one person, and that accountable person is the Vice President. In lieu of presenting 15 other witnesses, we will be presenting the Vice President herself for Article 1 of the Articles of Impeachment,” Kapunan said.

“In this game of chess, there are pawns, bishops, castles, and horses. And the most important, more important than the king, and I speak this not because of my gender, but the queen is more important than the king because the queen can move in many directions. And we have seen that. We have seen that in the evidence presented,” she added.

The prosecution was supposed to present at least three more witnesses on the alleged misuse of confidential funds, namely, Police Major Jovelyn Magay; Sunshine Fajarda, former Assistant Secretary of the Department of Education (DepEd) and incumbent Director VI of the OVP; and Commission on Audit- Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office Assistant Commissioner and Chief Executive Staff Bresilio Sabaldan.

Kapunan, however, said that the prosecution’s case as far as the confidential fund misuse is concerned is already clear “based on 4,750 documents presented and identified by the 12 witnesses, 10 of whom were present in court and subjected themselves to long cross-examinations by the defense counsels, and as well to questions from the senator-judges.”

In response to Kapunan’s take, defense lead counsel Sheila Sison said the Senate impeachment court compelling the Vice President to testify would violate the Constitution, which states that “No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself."

“This right is absolute, and this is not only a simple right or a statutory right. This is a fundamental right. This is a right emanating from the Constitution itself and one that emanates from the guarantees under Article 3 of our 1987 Constitution,” Sison said.
“If respondent is not interested in this trial, she would not have even sent her lawyers to defend her in this case,” she said.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said the prosecution should submit such a motion seeking a subpoena or court order for the Vice President to testify at her own trial first so the defense can comment and for the court to ultimately rule on it.

After this issue was tabled, public prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list disclosed that the prosecution filed a request for admission which seeks the Vice President’s admission on the authenticity and ownership of bank accounts, the records of which will be presented by the prosecution as evidence.

Diokno said such admission from the Vice President on ownership and authenticity of such bank accounts will greatly speed up the trial proceedings since she "necessarily possesses personal knowledge" of such accounts and "immediate means of verifying their accuracy and genuineness through her own records or directly with the banks that produced them."
Defense team lawyer Michael Poa asked for 15 days to reply to such request for admission submitted by the prosecution, a motion which the court granted.

With the prosecution deciding to rest its presentation of its witnesses on alleged misuse of confidential funds, senator-judge Erwin Tulfo took the time to call on the Senate impeachment court to decide if 16 should remain the voting threshold needed to secure a conviction of the Vice President.

Tulfo posed the question since Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained over separate plunder charges, while Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court.
Senator Loren Legarda, meanwhile, has not been attending the trial for weeks now due to health concerns, specifically a lung problem that she is having treated overseas.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Escudero then ruled that the court will hear amici curiae (friends of the court) on September 16 to weigh in on the voting threshold.
He also scheduled the oral arguments between the prosecution and the defense on the voting threshold and the senator-judges’ voting on the issue for September 23. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: US-Canada tariff dispute weighs on cross-border ties
articles.summary: As Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect, Canadian and US car industries fear the trade war will hit them hard, while Canadians are cutting back on travel.

image.caption: The Gordie Howe International Bridge links Windsor, Canada, with Detroit, Michigan. After US President Trump threatened to block its inauguration, it has become symbolic for fraying US-Canadian tiesImage: Dax Melmer/REUTERS

blocks.text: A new suspension bridge connecting the United States to Canada recently opened after more than two decades of planning, but only the Canadians showed up to celebrate.
The Gordie Howe International Bridge spans the Detroit River, connecting Detroit, Michigan with Windsor, Ontario. It is named after a Canadian hockey player who starred for a US team.
"In normal times, that would be a very, very big celebration, a grand event, with leaders of both countries present," Michigan auto industry spokesperson Glenn Stevens Junior told DW.
But these are hardly normal times in US-Canada relations.
'Escalating tariffs will harm workers'

In July, US President Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on a wide range of goods from Canada. A second Trump announcement days later of the doubling of tariffs on Canadian automobiles and auto parts to 50%triggered even more concern for businesses on both sides of the new bridge.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney countered with tariffs between 15% and 50% on $20 billion (€17.2 billion) worth of goods imported from the US.
US-Canada trade war: The cost of fighting back

The retaliatory measures took effect at 12.01 Eastern Standard Time (05:01 GMT/UST) on Tuesday September 8. Polls by the Canadian non-profit Angus Reid suggested that the majority of Canadians were in favor of a tougher stance in tariffs.
At the same time, Canadian workers feared for their jobs, the polls found.
Business leaders, too, have warned of the harmful effects of the tariffs on the economies of both countries.

"An escalating cycle of tariffs and retaliation will ultimately harm businesses, workers, and consumers on both sides of the border," the Detroit-based Canada and US Business Association (CUSBA) said in a statement in response to the tit-for-tat tariff hikes. "Each new tariff compounds costs, disrupts production, delays investment, and weakens the competitiveness of US and Canadian businesses."
Jobs at stake on both sides of the border
Further north, the Financial Accountability Office of Ontario estimated the new tariff regime will cost 119,000 local jobs in 2026.
Many of these are predicted to be in the auto industry, with Ontario's auto manufacturing output estimated to shrink by 8% in 2026 compared with a no-tariff scenario.

This contraction is expected to be felt on the US side too, especially in Michigan, where more than a fifth of all vehicles produced in the US in 2022 were built, including several well-known household brand names.
The economies of Michigan and Ontario are deeply interconnected, the Detroit Regional Chamber stressed in August.

"Engines that are built in Michigan go into trucks that are built in Ontario, engines that are built in Ontario go into trucks that are built into Michigan," said Glenn Stevens Jr, who is also the chamber's Chief Automotive and Innovation Officer.
Figures show that by 2023, Detroit automakers supported 815,000 indirect jobs through supply chains, as well as 147,000 direct workers across the US.
Detroit's chamber has called for a restoration of "normalcy," defined as a focus on the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, (USMCA, or CUSMA in Canada), due for an annual review.
Tariffs, EV attacks and AI blamed for job cuts
Even before the announcement of Trump's tariffs and Canada's counter-tariffs, Detroit's famous car industry had stalled.
The volume of production for companies was relatively stable as were jobs on and around auto factory lines, Stevens Jr said.
Although this meant there wasn't a significant loss in employment, new job opportunities weren't being created.
Analyzing the number of US car dealership franchise listings for new vehicles is a standard way of tracking auto production.
These listings show vehicle production has generally increased in the past 12 months, but the past 30 days show a significant slowdown.
Data from industry weekly Automotive News has around 33,000 more listed vehicles compared to this time last year, but 70,000 fewer vehicles were listed in the past month.
Can North America launch its own EV revolution?
Beyond the car showrooms, the US auto industry's cautionary approach is apparent.
US auto companies were adjusting business plans even before the latest round of tariff announcements, with business leaders warning of increased US manufacturing costs.
These costs have now been handed down to the consumers, with US shoppers seeing record sales prices of more than $52,000 for new cars in September.

Companies had resisted hiring people or expanding over the past 18 months since tariff talks between Canada and the US had started to intensify, Stevens Jr said, adding to a lack of investment in new designs owing to withdrawn US federal support for electric vehicles.
Is cross-border friendship fraying?
Apart from the auto industry, the tariffs are impacting other sectors.
Across the US, real estate market media in June described a "cooling relationship between the two countries," affecting property transactions, tourism revenue and the local economy.
"Most Canadians think it's unpatriotic ... to visit the United States," Claude Molineri, CEO of Visit Detroit said of the cooling friendship and downturn in tourism.
Earlier this year, Detroit's official visitor site reported that the city had seen an 11% decrease in Canadian guests compared to 2025.
Meanwhile, several "buy Canadian first" online campaigns have been referring users to local businesses and Canadian ingredients in everyday grocery items in response to the tariff enouncements.

The cities of Detroit and Ontario's Windsor/Essex normally facilitate trade worth more than $100 billion each year, which is almost a third of all annual trade between the US and Canada, according to Downtown Detroit Partnership, a group of business and community leaders.
The cooling ties between the two countries could come at a heavy price.
Why Canada rejected Trump's terms despite economic risks

items: Prince Harry and Meghan were surprised by a letter from King Charles confirming they are no longer working members of the royal family and will remain private citizens.
The couple returned to Britain after six years in the US, with their return being unexpected even to close family members.
The letter clarified that their charitable work is a personal matter and that they have maintained their financial independence and privacy since stepping down from royal duties.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

LONDON, United Kingdom – Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are surprised by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles clarifying that they were no longer working members of the royal family and that they would remain private citizens, their spokesperson said.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children returned to live in Britain last month, six years after stepping down from royal duties and moving to the US during a period of estrangement and awkward relations with the royal family.
The return was a surprise even to close family with Harry’s father, the king, only being told days before the news became public.
In a letter, authorized by Charles and sent to senior British officials on Monday, it was made clear that Harry and Meghan were no longer working members of the royal family.
A spokesperson for the couple said they had only been informed shortly before it was sent out and they were surprised by what had occurred.

The letter said their status, which was originally agreed with the late Queen Elizabeth in 2020, gave the couple personal latitude “in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish”.

“It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex…. The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity,” it said.
“In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”

Since leaving for the US, the couple have continued to make the headlines as Harry accused the royals of neglect, the tabloid press of ruining his life and the government of failing to provide automatic police protection which would allow him to return home.
A committee which decides on what level of security he should be afforded at public expense is due to meet this week to decide what protection he should have now his family have returned to Britain.
They have also struck a number of commercial deals, most notably with streaming giant Netflix, while Meghan has launched a lifestyle brand As Ever. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY — Unidentified gunmen shot and injured a village councilor in Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte at 11:40 a.m. on Tuesday, police said.

The attack that injured Rusman Agar Pinguiaman, 33, a resident of Barangay Baka, Datu Odin Sinsuat town, occurred while the election gun ban is in effect in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) for the first parliamentary elections on Sept. 14.

Capt. Steffi Salanguit, Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (PRO-BAR) spokesperson, said Pinguiaman was taking a coffee break at a roadside restaurant when two men on a motorbike arrived.
Salaguit said one of them pulled a pistol and shot the village official in his chest.
The suspects immediately fled.
Relatives rushed him to the Cotabato Regional and Medical Center in Cotabato City.
Salanguit said the motive of the attack and the perpetrators remained unknown and investigation is continuing.

articles.summary: BALANGA CITY, Bataan – Bataan’s component city and its low-lying villages were once again inundated by massive floods following continuous rains from Monday afternoon (September 7) until…

blocks.text: BALANGA CITY, Bataan – Bataan’s component city and its low-lying villages were once again inundated by massive floods following continuous rains from Monday afternoon (September 7) until Tuesday morning (September 8).
Although rains tapered off on Tuesday, Barangays Puerto Rivas, Sibacan and populous Tenejero were still under two to three feet of floodwaters as of posting time.
Some portions of Roman Highway were under knee-high floodwaters but passable to all vehicles.

In a consultation meeting of the Bataan provincial government and the Department of Public Works and Highways, high waters were traced to Dinalupihan town where a landslide had swept away nine houses.
The DPWH and provincial engineers discovered that the landslide blanketed the small waterways, some of the rivers and a creek in Dinalupihan.
The massive erosion had uprooted trees, and the resulting debris fell ended up in the Pita River.

To curb Bataan flooding, the local government will tap experts to adopt science-based and nature-based solutions using hazard and terrain assessment, satellite data, drone and aerial surveys, as well as watershed rehabilitation and the restoration of waterways. /gsg

articles.title: Despite red alert, no power outages happened in Oriental Mindoro
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Oriental Mindoro Grid was placed under Red Alert on September 7 (Monday) due to a projected supply deficit. But no power interruption was implemented as the…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Oriental Mindoro Grid was placed under Red Alert on September 7 (Monday) due to a projected supply deficit.
But no power interruption was implemented as the actual power situation turned out better than what was initially forecast, the Oriental Mindoro Electric Cooperative (ORMECO) reported.

ORMECO General Manager Humphrey Dolor attributed the favorable outcome to higher-than-expected supply from Independent Power Producers (IPPs) and lower actual electricity demand driven by cooler weather.
“While we issued a Red Alert and stood ready for load shedding based on the best data we had that morning, reality proved more favorable,” Dolor said.
The electric cooperative official explained that supply providers delivered more power than projected, and consumption stayed lower than estimated.
This combination of factors kept the cooperative above critical levels and there was no need to resort to strategic brownouts or Manual Load Dropping (MLD) .

Had circumstances been different, ORMECO would have enforced MLD or programmed rotational brownouts used by grid operators to temporarily cut electricity in specific areas when power supply is lower than consumer demand.
The cooperative observed that the tightest supply-demand margin was recorded at 2:00 p.m. at just 4.35 megawatts — close enough to trigger interruptions but was ultimately manageable.
Nine feeder interruption incidents occurred during the critical period, but all were restored within the day, with most back in service in six minutes or less.
“Manual Load Dropping is always a last resort. We only implement it when absolutely necessary to protect the grid,” Dolor said in a message on Tuesday.
“Yesterday, we remained on alert, but our generation partners and weather conditions worked in our favor, and our response teams restored faults almost immediately,” the official added. /apl

articles.title: 2 fishermen nabbed for illegal compressor fishing in Romblon
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) apprehended two fishermen who were allegedly engaged in illegal fishing using a compressor as an underwater breathing apparatus off Barangay Danao in…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) apprehended two fishermen who were allegedly engaged in illegal fishing using a compressor as an underwater breathing apparatus off Barangay Danao in Cajidiocan, Romblon.

The Search and Rescue (SAR) Team of Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Cajidiocan spotted the suspicious motorbanca on its way back to its sub-station after searching for missing fishermen amid unfavorable weather conditions.
The team approached the boat and found the two fishermen, both residents of Barangay Cambalo in Cajidiocan, allegedly using a compressor while underwater to catch fish.
The PCG said the fishing method violated Municipal Ordinance No. 03-11, Section 67, or the Comprehensive Fishery Ordinance of Cajidiocan.
The fishermen were informed of the alleged violation and apprised of their constitutional rights.

Confiscated during the operation were a motorized fishing boat and engine, compressor engine, aluminum air tank compressor, a pair of flippers, spear guns, about 100 meters of hose, 15 kilograms of assorted fish, goggles and a flashlight.
The fishermen were placed under the Coast Guard’s temporary custody while the confiscated items were properly secured.
The PCG said the boat and other confiscated items would be turned over to the Cajidiocan Municipal Agriculture Office for appropriate administrative action.
Two fishermen apprehended for illegal compressor fishing in Romblon (Photo courtesy of the Coast Guard)

articles.title: FACT CHECK: No, Malabon congressman Oreta did not wish for Sara Duterte’s death
articles.summary: In an email to Rappler, the lawmaker's office said Oreta did not make the alleged statement. He also cautioned the public to be wary of posts circulating online.

blocks.text: Claim: Malabon City Representative Antolin “Lenlen” Oreta III wished death upon Vice President Sara Duterte.
Why we fact-checked this: The quote attributing the statement to the congressman was posted on September 7 by a Facebook page named “Malabon Standard,” which currently has over 10,000 followers.
As of writing, the post has more than 94,000 reactions, 42,500 comments, and 3,600 shares.
The post quotes Oreta allegedly saying, “Wala akong pake kung you do not feel safe Inday Sara, sana mamatay ka na.”
(I don’t care if you don’t feel safe, Inday Sara. I hope you die.)
The quote has since been reposted by various pages and accounts on social media.
The facts: Oreta did not make the statement attributed to him in the post. His media office confirmed this in an email to Rappler on Tuesday, September 8.
“We would like to clarify that Congressman Oreta did not make this statement. The quote is fabricated and is being falsely attributed to him,” his office said.

In a Facebook post on September 7, Oreta labeled the circulating quote as false. He cautioned users online to be wary of pages and posts that use his image and name, and to check official sources for verification.
Oreta was among the 257 lawmakers who voted to impeach Duterte for a second time.

‘I do not feel safe’: The fabricated quote appears to be a response to Duterte’s remarks when she arrived at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on September 5 to post bail, after the court ordered her arrest on three counts of grave threats over her alleged assassination threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his relatives.

While at the court to post her P360,000 bail — P120,000 for each count — she expressed concern for her safety, repeatedly claiming that she doesn’t trust the authorities and wanted to bring people, including the media, inside the court.
“I do not feel safe. I do not feel safe anywhere. Pumunta lang ako [rito] kasi sabi ninyo pupunta ako sa court (I only went here because you told me I needed to appear in court),” Duterte said.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla responded to Duterte’s statements, saying the Philippine National Police “accorded her all the respect her position deserves” and that they have a copy of all police body cam footage from Duterte’s arrival until her posting of bail.

Duterte has been claiming that there are security threats against her. According to her impeachment lawyers, there is a threat against the Duterte family called “Operation Romanov,” a reference to the execution of Russia’s last imperial family. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

More than 12,000 barangays nationwide are susceptible to rain-induced landslides and flood due to the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) said Tuesday.
There are 12,161 barangays susceptible to geohazards from September 8 to 11 based on the rainfall forecasts of the state weather bureau PAGASA, according to the bureau.
As of 8 a.m. of Tuesday, September 8, the landslide- and flood-prone barangays are located in the following regions:

items: Ilocos Region - 1,558
Cagayan Valley - 1,519
Cordillera Administrative Region - 774
National Capital Region - 1,403
Central Luzon - 2,709
Calabarzon - 2,476
Mimaropa - 572
Bicol Region - 1,088
Western Visayas - 29
Eastern Visayas - 33

blocks.text: "Based on the latest DOST-PAGASA 72-hour rainfall forecast, residents in listed areas and those nearby or downstream are urged to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions," the MGB said.
Geohazard susceptibility maps are produced based on local geology, landforms and terrains, and human activities that could elevate disaster risks.

The barangay lists are generated using rainfall forecast data from PAGASA, rain-induced landslide and flooding susceptibility maps from DENR-MGB, and barangay boundaries from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), according to the bureau.

blocks.text: Trump says Canada's Bombardier must build jets in US or lose market access
President Donald Trump said that ⁠Canadian private jet maker Bombardier would ⁠no longer be allowed ​to sell its planes in the United States unless it started manufacturing in the country.
“NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.
“If ⁠they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank’,” he said.

Trump made the post as a trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa esclates, part of the near-global tariff wall in his second term ⁠that has drawn complaints from many US trading partners. Canada is set to introduce a wave of counter-tariffs against the US on Tuesday.

Bombardier, the Montreal-based rival of US business jet manufacturer Gulfstream Aerospace, has an American workforce of 3,500, and a US footprint of 2,800 suppliers, along with factories and service centers in the country.
The company is now adding its sixth US service center and produces wings for its flagship Global 8000 jet in Texas.
New Hampshire and Rhode Island electorate to vote in state primaries
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
New Hampshire and Rhode Island primary voters will choose candidates across a full slate of federal, state and local offices over the next two days.

In New Hampshire, US senator Jeanne Shaheen’s decision to not seek reelection created a cascade of competitive races, AP reported. Two of the eight Republicans hoping to replace the three-term Democrat are former US senators she previously defeated: John E. Sununu and Scott Brown.
The five-way race for the Democratic nomination includes US representative Chris Pappas, whose departure from his 1st congressional district seat in turn attracted a crowd of candidates.

Shaheen’s daughter, Stefany Shaheen, is among those seeking the Democratic nomination for Pappas’ seat, along with former candidate Maura Sullivan. Several other candidates in top races also are making repeat appearances.

Meanwhile, in Rhode Island, governor Dan McKee faces a tough Democratic primary challenge tomorrow in his bid for a second full term. Voters will also choose nominees for a full slate of federal, state and local offices.

McKee was elected governor by a wide margin in 2022 after first assuming the role in March 2021 when then-governor Gina Raimondo stepped down to become US commerce secretary. He now is at risk of becoming the nation’s first elected governor since 2014 to lose renomination and the first in Rhode Island since 1994.

His challenger is Helena Buonanno Foulkes, a former longtime executive with Rhode Island-based CVS. She placed a close second behind McKee in the five-way 2022 Democratic primary. She is the niece of former Democratic senator Chris Dodd of Connecticut.

articles.title: Jojo Ang’s 4 out of 14 graft cases consolidated in Sandiganbayan
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Four out of the 14 counts of graft charges against Uswag Ilonggo party-list Rep. Jojo Ang are now consolidated in the Sandiganbayan Second Division. Ang’s counsel Luis Veracruz…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Four out of the 14 counts of graft charges against Uswag Ilonggo party-list Rep. Jojo Ang are now consolidated in the Sandiganbayan Second Division.

Ang’s counsel Luis Veracruz said the anti-graft court’s Fourth Division issued a resolution allowing the consolidation of the two counts of graft the said division had handled to the Second Division, which is also handling two other counts.
“Four cases [were consolidated] in just two divisions, the rest are pending,” Veracruz said in an ambush interview.
In his arraignment, Ang pleaded not guilty to both counts of graft under the Second Division.
His pretrial was supposed to proceed after his arraignment.
However, Presiding Justice Geralinde Faith Econg, the Second Division chair, rescheduled the pretrial to Sept. 15 due to the Fourth Division’s granting of consolidation.
“The records [from the Fourth Division] were not yet endorsed to the Second Division,” Veracruz said.
Prosecutors indicted Ang for alleged violation of Section 3(h) of Republic Act 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
Ang allegedly had a stake in a construction firm that won P214 million in public works contracts while being a sitting party-list representative. /das

articles.title: Indigenous protesters block Benguet mine with vegetable trucks
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — Indigenous protesters in the Benguet mining town of Mankayan lined up vegetable delivery trucks along a road to block the entrance to Crescent Mining Development Corp. (CMDC) on Monday.…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — Indigenous protesters in the Benguet mining town of Mankayan lined up vegetable delivery trucks along a road to block the entrance to Crescent Mining Development Corp. (CMDC) on Monday.
They wanted to prevent court officials, company employees, and police from serving them a writ of preliminary injunction against the year-long barricade at Barangay Bulalacao.
Court officials brought the writ issued on August 20 by Regional Trial Court Judge Daniel Mangallay of Branch 64 in Abatan, Buguias.

In his 15-page resolution, Mangallay ordered protesters to “immediately remove all forms of barricades” along the Guinaoang-Colocol Road and barred them from preventing CMDC employees, vehicles, equipment, and machinery from entering and conducting drilling operations.

He also directed personnel of the Mankayan Municipal Police Station, the Philippine National Police’s 1st Provincial Mobile Force Company, and nearby police stations to assist the acting sheriff and CMDC employees in implementing the writ and, if warranted, arrest and file appropriate charges against those who defy the order.
But the court first required CMDC to post a P500,000 bond.
But residents of Bulalacao and neighboring Guinaoang refused to dismantle their barricade, which they have been maintaining since October 2025.

The community first blocked CMDC’s drilling operations in June 2022 after the company’s Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) expired. They again barricaded the road in August 2025, thwarting the company’s attempt to bring in heavy equipment, before setting up another barricade in October that has since remained in place.
Residents say the barricade was their last resort to protect their farmlands, water sources and livelihood while their petitions against the mine remain pending before government agencies.
They questioned the renewal of CMDC’s MPSA, saying it was granted without the required Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) of affected indigenous communities.

CMDC, however, maintains that its MPSA remains valid. The company says it complied with the FPIC process, which resulted in a memorandum of agreement with indigenous communities represented by their Council of Elders.
As of press time, court officials and the police have pulled back from the standoff at noon while protesters attended Mass held at the protest site./coa

articles.title: Mother flagged faulty smoke alarms before house fire that killed father and five children, court hears
articles.summary:
Pre-inquest conference into Queensland deaths hears witnesses did not hear any smoke alarms during 2023 fire

  • Get our

blocks.text: A landlord was repeatedly warned about improperly installed smoke alarms before a house fire that killed a father and five children in Queensland in 2023, a coroner has heard.
Deputy state coroner Donald MacKenzie held a pre-inquest conference into the Russell Island deaths on Tuesday.
No witness recalls hearing the sound of an alarm during the blaze, it heard.
The owner was fined $774 for improper installation in 2024, the maximum possible penalty under Queensland law. A conviction was not recorded.
The fire in the two-storey wooden Queenslander broke out on 6 August 2023. The house had been moved to the island and then renovated in 2013 before being rented privately.

Five children – two brothers aged four and others aged three, 10 and 11 – died in the blaze. Their father, 34, died after running into the fire to rescue them. None can be identified for legal reasons.
The children’s mother and father had fallen asleep in a converted “chill out” area underneath the house.
The father awoke to see thick black smoke and immediately raced upstairs, where the children were sleeping.
His partner also tried to get into the house, but was forced back by the fire. Another adult woman leapt off a balcony to safety and survived.
The Queensland fire department does not have a station on Russell Island, and vehicles must be ferried over in an emergency, a process that takes about 45-60 minutes, the court heard.
As a result, it was a paramedic who first arrived at the scene, arriving within minutes at about 6.26am.

“He recalls that the fire’s heat was so intense that he could feel it through his vehicle window, and could see the flames coming from the roof and smoke in a mushroom formation,” counsel assisting Corinne Leach told the court.

“[The children’s mother] was kneeling on the ground in complete distress with [the other woman] beside her. He asked if anyone else was inside, to which [the mother} replied: her five children, and lost all ability to communicate.”
The paramedic also tried to get into the building but was halted by the intense blaze. He instead focused on evacuating neighbouring homes. Rural firefighters arrived at 6.35am.

The court heard the home had poor wiring, an exposed electrical box and faulty power points, known to short out. It also had an extension cord running from a poorly operating power point in a child’s bedroom, from a double adapter, to the understory area.
The home’s smoke alarms also had not been updated in compliance with 2017 laws that applied to any tenancy renewed after January 2022 imposing additional safety measures for alarms.
The homeowner claimed not to have been aware of the legislative change, the court heard.
“[The mother] says that she raised the issue of non-working smoke alarms with the home’s owner, but nothing was done about it,” Leach told the court.
“No witness recalls hearing a smoke alarm sounding at all prior or during the fire.”

MacKenzie has been tasked with investigating seven issues, including whether legally installed fire alarms might have prevented the deaths, and whether the emergency service response to the fire was adequate.
He will also consider whether the presence of any additional emergency service resources located on the island could have prevented the deaths.
Fire investigators have been unable to identify the cause of the blaze, and could not categorically rule out that it was lit deliberately, the court heard.
The inquest has been listed to sit for 10 days in November, to hear from 16 witnesses.
